resources.title: Identity
resources.intro: Who a token is, and what that person may do.

resources.title: Read-only token API
resources.intro: Three reads under `/api/public-v1` that accept an API token and nothing else. They are the simplest way to list projects and tasks. Every read is narrowed to what the token's person can open in the web app, and a token limited to projects reads only those.

resources.title: Tasks
resources.intro: Creating a task and changing one. Both routes take the bodies the web app sends, so their field names follow the stored task. To read tasks, use [Everything](#everything) or the [Read-only token API](#read-only-token-api).

resources.title: Everything
resources.intro: One list of tasks across every project the caller can read, with filters, grouping, sorting and a cursor, and the caller's saved views of that list.

resources.title: Projects
resources.intro: Duplicating a project, and saving a project as a template to start others from. To list projects, use `GET /api/public-v1/projects`.

resources.title: Pages
resources.intro: Docs and wiki pages, their version history, and who a comment on one can name. A page belongs to a project or to the workspace. A private page is its author's alone; any other page is open to whoever can see its project. A page the caller cannot see answers the same as one that does not exist.

resources.title: Agents
resources.intro: Read-only views of the workspace's AI agents: who they are, what they are running and what they have proposed. Runs and proposals are narrowed to the projects and tasks the caller can read.

resources.title: Dashboards
resources.intro: The answers of the Ask cards on a dashboard. These two routes sit under `/api/v1`; they are described here because a token can call them.

resources.title: Webhooks
resources.intro: Managing the webhooks described under [Webhook deliveries](#webhook-deliveries) above. A webhook belongs to the person who created it: nobody else can list, change or delete it, or read its delivery log.

resources.title: Goals
resources.intro: Goals with targets that show how far a team or a person has got. A goal has an owner, a period and up to 20 targets; its progress is the weighted average of its targets. A target is a `number`, a `currency` amount, a `boolean` or a `tasks` target counted from lists and tasks. A goal is `private` (its owner), `people` (its owner and the people it is shared with) or `workspace` (every member; a guest only when named). Guests can read goals shared with them and cannot create one. A token limited to projects cannot use these routes. A write made with an agent's token follows the rules that hold that agent.

resources.title: Whiteboards
resources.intro: One whiteboard for each list: task cards, sticky notes and text laid out on a canvas. A board is as open as its list: it can be read by whoever can open the list, and changed by whoever can edit the project while the list, its folders and the project are active. The title of a task card is shown only to someone who may open that task.

resources.title: Imports
resources.intro: Undoing an import that created tasks in bulk.

resources.title: Custom fields
resources.intro: Reading the tasks a relationship field links and the votes on a voting field, and casting a vote.

GET /api/v2/api-tokens/me.title: Who am I
GET /api/v2/api-tokens/me.summary: Returns the person and the workspace behind the token, with that person's role and permissions.
description: Call it once after connecting, to check that the token and the `companyid` header are right.

responseFields.name: roleType
responseFields.description: `1` is the owner, `2` an admin, `3` a member, `0` a guest.

responseFields.name: permissions
responseFields.description: The person's workspace-wide answer for the permission keys the server checks most: `true` may change, `false` may only read, `null` has no access, and `1` or `2` mean "own" or "everyone" on the keys that take a choice. A project with its own rules can answer differently.

responseFields.name: scopes
responseFields.description: The token's scopes. Empty when the request was made with a session.

GET /api/public-v1/projects.title: List projects
GET /api/public-v1/projects.summary: Lists the projects the token's person can open.
description: Called with an API token that holds the `read` scope, for a person who is still a member of the workspace. Answers with `data`: up to 200 projects that are not deleted and that the token's person can open, each with `ProjectName`, `ProjectCode` and `createdAt`.
responseNotes: There is no `statusText` on a success here. Projects in the trash are left out.
GET /api/public-v1/projects.paging: None. At most 200 projects are returned.

GET /api/public-v1/tasks.title: List a project's tasks
GET /api/public-v1/tasks.summary: Lists the tasks of one project, most recently updated first.
description: Called with an API token that holds the `read` scope. It reads the query field `projectId` (a 24-character id, required) and `limit` (a number, clamped to 1 to 500, 100 when left out); a missing or malformed `projectId` answers 400, and a project the token's person cannot open answers 404. Answers with `data`: the project's tasks that are not deleted, most recently updated first, each with `TaskKey`, `TaskName`, `status`, `statusType`, `Task_Priority`, `AssigneeUserId`, `DueDate`, `sprintId`, `epicId`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.

query.name: projectId
query.description: The project.

query.name: limit
query.description: How many tasks to return, from 1 to 500. 100 when left out.

responseNotes: Each task carries these fields and `epicId` when it has one, and no others. Deleted tasks are left out, and so are tasks in lists the person cannot see.
GET /api/public-v1/tasks.paging: Limit only. There is no next page: narrow by project and raise `limit`, or use `POST /api/v2/tasks/everything` to page.

errors.400: `projectId` is missing or is not an id.
errors.404: The project does not exist, or the person cannot see it.

GET /api/public-v1/tasks/:key.title: Read a task by its key
GET /api/public-v1/tasks/:key.summary: Returns one task, looked up by its key.
description: Called with an API token that holds the `read` scope. The path value is the task key as a string of at most 40 characters; an empty or longer one answers 400, and a task the token's person cannot open or that does not exist answers 404. Answers with `data`: the stored task.

pathParams.name: key
pathParams.description: The task's key, for example `WEB-12`. At most 40 characters.

responseNotes: `data` is the whole stored task; the example shows some of its fields.

errors.400: The key is longer than 40 characters.
errors.404: No task has that key, or the person cannot see it.

POST /api/v2/tasks.title: Create a task
POST /api/v2/tasks.summary: Creates a task, or a subtask when `data.ParentTaskId` names a parent.
description: The body is the one the web app sends: the task under `data` and the project it goes into under `projectData`. The server sets the company and the acting person itself, whatever the body says. Under a parent, the project, list and folder are taken from the parent, and the parent must be in the project the body names.
The task's key is assigned after the task is saved, from the project's code and its next number. Read the task back to learn it.

body.name: data.TaskName
body.description: The task's name.

body.name: data.TaskKey
body.description: A placeholder such as `-`. The server replaces it with the real key.

body.name: data.TaskType
body.description: One of the project's task types, by its value.

body.name: data.TaskTypeKey
body.description: The key of that task type.

body.name: data.ProjectID
body.description: The project the task goes into.

body.name: data.sprintId
body.description: The list the task goes into.

body.name: data.sprintArray
body.description: `{ id, name }` of that list, with `folderId` and `folderName` when the list sits in a folder.

body.name: data.folderObjId
body.description: The folder, when the list sits in one.

body.name: data.status
body.description: The status as the project defines it: `{ text, key, type }`.

body.name: data.statusKey
body.description: The key of that status.

body.name: data.statusType
body.description: The type of that status, for example `default_active`.

body.name: data.Task_Priority
body.description: The priority, for example `MEDIUM`.

body.name: data.AssigneeUserId
body.description: The assignees. Each must hold a seat in the workspace.

body.name: data.watchers
body.description: The watchers. Each must hold a seat in the workspace.

body.name: data.Task_Leader
body.description: The task's lead. Must hold a seat in the workspace.

body.name: data.DueDate
body.description: The due date, or an empty string. With a date, send `data.dueDateDeadLine` as `[{ date }]`.

body.name: data.startDate
body.description: The start date.

body.name: data.ParentTaskId
body.description: The parent, for a subtask. Empty for a top-level task.

body.name: data.isParentTask
body.description: `true` for a top-level task, `false` for a subtask.

body.name: data.deletedStatusKey
body.description: `0` for a live task.

body.name: projectData._id
body.description: The same project as `data.ProjectID`.

body.name: projectData.ProjectName
body.description: The project's name, used in the notification.

body.name: projectData.ProjectCode
body.description: The project's code. The task's key starts with it.

body.name: indexObj
body.description: Where the task sits in the web app's grouped lists: `{ indexName, searchKey, searchValue }`. `indexName` is one of `groupByStatusIndex`, `groupByPriorityIndex`, `groupByAssigneeIndex`, `groupByDueDateIndex`.

bodyNotes: `data` may carry any other field a stored task has. A field a task does not have is dropped. `_id`, `createdBy` and `createdAt` are refused.
responseNotes: The new task's id is in `id`, beside `status`, not inside `data`.

errors.400: The body is not an object, carries a key that is not accepted, names something that is not an id where an id is expected, names a person who holds no seat in the workspace, the parent cannot take another level of subtasks, or the workspace's plan allows no more tasks in the list.
errors.404: The parent task does not exist, or is not in the project the body names.

PATCH /api/v2/tasks.title: Change a task
PATCH /api/v2/tasks.summary: Changes one task. `action` names the change, and the other keys of the body depend on it.
description: Each action reads the task it changes from the id shown under Ids, and answers 404 when the caller cannot see that task. The first id listed is the task; the others are the further tasks, people or projects the action names.

The server fills in the acting person, the company and, where an action uses them, the stored names of the task and its project. Keys an action does not use are dropped rather than refused, so the bodies the web app sends keep working. Where a key is followed by names in brackets, those are the only fields of that object the action writes.
Some actions take `isUpdateTask`. Leave it out. Sent as `false` it records history for a change another request already made, and is refused with 409 unless the stored task already holds that value.

body.name: action
body.description: One of the actions in the table below.

actionNotes.updateStatus: Sets the status. `newStatus` holds the status as the project defines it.
actionNotes.updateTaskCustomField: Sets one custom field's value: `customFieldId`, and `updateDetail` with the field's id as `_id` and the value as `fieldValue`. A value that does not fit the field's type is refused.
actionNotes.updateArchiveDelete: `deletedStatusKey` `1` deletes and needs `task.task_delete`, `2` archives and needs `task.task_archive`, `0` restores and needs `task.task_list`.
actionNotes.updateChecklists: Assigning or unassigning an item needs `task.task_checklist_assign_remove`. Every other operation needs `task.task_checklist`.
actionNotes.moveTask: The key is also needed in the project the task moves to.
actionNotes.duplicateTask: The key is also needed in the project the copy goes to.
actionNotes.mergeTask: The key is also needed in the destination project.

responseNotes: `data` is what the action itself answered, and differs from action to action. An action that found nothing to change answers `status: false` with its reason.

firebaseObj.TaskName: Write and review the release notes

errors.400: No `action`, an action that is not accepted, something that is not an id where an id is expected, a key that is not accepted, a value that does not fit the field, or a person named who holds no seat in the workspace.
errors.404: The task does not exist or the caller cannot see it. For a move or a copy, the destination project does not exist.
errors.409: `isUpdateTask` was `false` and the stored task does not hold the value the request names.

POST /api/v2/tasks/everything.title: List tasks across projects
POST /api/v2/tasks/everything.summary: Lists tasks from every project the caller can read, filtered, grouped, sorted and paged.
description: It is a read sent as a `POST`, so a token needs the `write` scope. Every key of the body is optional, and an unknown key at any level is a 400.

Whatever the body says, the server reads only projects the caller can open and whose task list their role may read, leaves out closed, archived and restricted projects, other people's personal lists, private lists the caller is not on, and deleted or archived tasks.

body.name: filter.status
body.description: Up to 100 status names or whole-number keys. Names match exactly.

body.name: filter.statusType
body.description: Any of `default_active`, `active`, `done`, `close`, `default_close`.

body.name: filter.assignee
body.description: Up to 100 user ids, or `unassigned`.

body.name: filter.priority
body.description: Up to 100 priority names.

body.name: filter.dueDate
body.description: `{ from, to, none }`. `from` and `to` are ISO dates or times in milliseconds. `none: true` means "no due date" and cannot be combined with a range.

body.name: filter.taskType
body.description: Up to 100 task type names or keys.

body.name: filter.tags
body.description: Up to 100 tag ids.

body.name: filter.search
body.description: Text of at most 200 characters.

body.name: filter.projectIds
body.description: Up to 500 project ids. It can only narrow what the caller may read.

body.name: filter.sprintIds
body.description: Up to 100 list ids: tasks that live in one of them or were added to one. A list the caller cannot open is ignored.

body.name: group
body.description: `none`, `status`, `assignee`, `project`, `priority` or `dueDate`. `none` when left out.

body.name: sort
body.description: `{ by, dir }`. `by` is `updatedAt` or `DueDate`; `dir` is `asc` or `desc`. Newest update first when left out; `DueDate` defaults to `asc`.

body.name: cursor
body.description: The `nextCursor` of the page before.

body.name: limit
body.description: A whole number from 1. 50 when left out, and never more than 100.

body.name: includeSubtasks
body.description: `false` when left out: top-level tasks only.

body.name: includeClosedProjects
body.description: `false` when left out. `true` adds back closed projects only.

body.name: timezone
body.description: An IANA timezone name, used for due-date groups. `UTC` when left out.

responseFields.name: rows
responseFields.description: Up to `limit` tasks. Each carries `_id`, `TaskName`, `TaskKey`, `status`, `statusKey`, `statusType`, `Task_Priority`, `AssigneeUserId`, `DueDate`, `startDate`, `ProjectID`, `sprintId`, `folderObjId`, `TaskType`, `TaskTypeKey`, `tagsArray`, `subTasks`, `ancestors`, `ParentTaskId`, `isParentTask`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `sprintArray` (the list the task lives in, with its `name`). A task that was added to other lists also carries `extraLists`: each entry has `projectId`, `sprintId`, `addedBy` and `addedAt`, and `name` and `projectName` only for a list the caller can open. No custom field values.

responseFields.name: groups
responseFields.description: On the first page, a list of `{ key, count }` for the chosen `group`, counted over the same filter. `key` is `null` for "no value". With `group: none` it holds one entry with the total. On a later page it is `null`.

responseFields.name: nextCursor
responseFields.description: A string when more rows exist, otherwise `null`.

responseFields.name: projects
responseFields.description: A map by project id, for the projects the rows name. Each carries `_id`, `ProjectName`, `ProjectCode`, `projectIcon`, `taskStatusData`, `taskTypeCounts`, `apps`, `statusType`, `isPersonal` and `edit: { status, priority }`, which says whether the caller may change those two fields on that project's tasks. With `group: project` it also names every project counted; one that has no row on the page carries only `_id`, `ProjectName`, `ProjectCode`, `projectIcon`, `statusType` and `isPersonal`.

POST /api/v2/tasks/everything.paging: Cursor. Send `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. A cursor is good only for the same workspace, person, filter, sort and the two `include` switches; with anything else it is a 400. The page size and the grouping may change between pages. Rows with no value for the sort key come last, in both directions.

errors.400: An unknown key, a wrong type, a value out of range, or a cursor that does not fit the request. The body is `{ status: false, statusText: "Request refused", message, field }`.
errors.403: The person holds no active seat in the workspace.

GET /api/v2/tasks/everything/views.title: List saved views
GET /api/v2/tasks/everything/views.summary: Lists the caller's own saved views of the Everything list, by name.
description: Any signed-in person with an active seat in the workspace may call it, and it lists only the views that person saved. Answers with `data`, sorted by name, each view with `_id`, `name`, `settings`, `isDefault` and `updatedAt`.

errors.403: The person holds no active seat in the workspace.

POST /api/v2/tasks/everything/views.title: Save a view
POST /api/v2/tasks/everything/views.summary: Saves a view: a name and the settings of the Everything list.
description: A view belongs to the person who made it. A person can keep at most 50.

body.name: name
body.description: 1 to 80 characters.

body.name: settings
body.description: An object with any of: `mode` (`list`, `board`, `table`), `search` (up to 200 characters), `status`, `assignee`, `priority`, `taskType` (lists of up to 100), `projectIds` (up to 500 ids), `due` (`overdue`, `today`, `week`, `later`, `none` or empty), `group` (`none`, `status`, `assignee`, `project`, `priority`, `dueDate`), `sortBy` (`updatedAt`, `DueDate`), `sortDir` (`asc`, `desc`), `showSubtasks`, `hideDone`, `includeClosed` (each `true` or `false`). An unknown key is refused.

body.name: isDefault
body.description: Makes this the view the page opens with. Only one view is the default.

errors.400: An unknown key, a missing or malformed field, or a value a setting does not take. The body names the `field`.
errors.403: The person holds no active seat in the workspace.

PATCH /api/v2/tasks/everything/views/:id.title: Change a saved view
PATCH /api/v2/tasks/everything/views/:id.summary: Changes the name, the settings or the default mark of one of the caller's views.
description: Any signed-in person with an active seat in the workspace may call it, on a view that person saved; any other id answers 404. Reads `name` (string), `settings` (object) and `isDefault` (boolean) from the body, and changes the ones sent. Making a view the default clears the mark on the caller's other views. Answers with `data`: the view as it is now.

body.name: name
body.description: 1 to 80 characters.

body.name: settings
body.description: Replaces the stored settings. The same keys as when saving a view.

body.name: isDefault
body.description: Makes this the default view, or stops it being the default.

bodyNotes: At least one of the three is required.

request.name: My open work, by due date

data.name: My open work, by due date

errors.400: An unknown key, a missing or malformed field, or a value a setting does not take. The body names the `field`.
errors.403: The person holds no active seat in the workspace.
errors.404: The view does not exist, or is someone else's.

DELETE /api/v2/tasks/everything/views/:i.title: Delete a saved view
DELETE /api/v2/tasks/everything/views/:i.summary: Deletes one of the caller's views.
description: Any signed-in person with an active seat in the workspace may call it, on a view that person saved; any other id answers 404. The view is marked deleted and leaves the list, and its default mark is cleared. Answers with `statusText` `View deleted.` and no `data`.

errors.403: The person holds no active seat in the workspace.
errors.404: The view does not exist, or is someone else's.

GET /api/v2/tasks/:id/lists.title: List a task's extra lists
GET /api/v2/tasks/:id/lists.summary: Lists the other lists a task has been added to, besides its own.
description: The ids are always given. A list's name and its project's name are given only for a live list the caller can open.
GET /api/v2/tasks/:id/lists.permission: The task must be one the caller can open

errors.400: The id is not an id.
errors.404: The task does not exist, or the caller cannot open it.

POST /api/v2/projects/:id/duplicate.title: Duplicate a project
POST /api/v2/projects/:id/duplicate.summary: Copies a project: its settings, folders, lists and automations, and its tasks when asked.
description: The copy gets a new project code. Automations are copied switched off. Custom fields are shared with the copy, not duplicated. A personal list cannot be duplicated.

Up to 300 tasks are copied before the answer. More than that are copied afterwards as a job: the answer carries the job, and `GET /api/v2/projects/:id/duplicate` on the copy reports how far it has got.
POST /api/v2/projects/:id/duplicate.permission: The project must be one the caller can open

body.name: name
body.description: The copy's name, at most 255 characters.

body.name: include.tasks
body.description: Copy the tasks.

body.name: include.assignees
body.description: Keep the assignees of the copied tasks.

body.name: include.dates
body.description: Keep the dates of the project, its lists and its tasks.

responseFields.name: project
responseFields.description: The whole stored copy; the example shows some of its fields.

responseFields.name: counts
responseFields.description: What was copied. `tasks` is `0` when the tasks are being copied as a job.

responseFields.name: notes
responseFields.description: What was left out or changed, each with a `code` and a `count` or a `name`: `tasks_left_out`, `private_lists_left`, `automations_skipped`, `automations_disabled`, `subfolder_moved_to_top`.

responseFields.name: sharedFields
responseFields.description: The ids of the custom fields now shared with the copy.

responseFields.name: job
responseFields.description: `null`, or `{ id, status, total, processed, created }` when the tasks are copied after the answer.

errors.400: The body is missing `name` or `include`, carries another key, a flag is not `true` or `false`, or the project is a personal list.
errors.404: The project does not exist, is in the trash, or the caller cannot see it.

GET /api/v2/projects/:id/duplicate.title: Read a duplicate's progress
GET /api/v2/projects/:id/duplicate.summary: Reports how far the tasks of a large copy have got.
description: Needs a project the caller can open. The path id is the copy that a `POST /api/v2/projects/:id/duplicate` made. Answers with `data`: the newest copy job that the caller started for that project, as `id`, `status`, `total`, `processed` and `created`, or `null` when there is none.
GET /api/v2/projects/:id/duplicate.permission: The project must be one the caller can open

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: The copy, not the project it was copied from.

responseNotes: `status` is `processing`, `done` or `failed`. `data` is `null` when the caller started no copy job for that project.

errors.404: The project does not exist, or the caller cannot see it.

POST /api/v2/projects/:id/template.title: Save a project as a template
POST /api/v2/projects/:id/template.summary: Saves a project's settings, folders, lists and, when asked, its tasks and automations as a template.
description: The template keeps no ids of the project it came from. Tasks start in the project's first status, with nothing ticked. A template holds at most 2000 tasks and a workspace at most 100 templates. A personal list cannot be saved.

A template is offered to everyone unless the project has a private list or `everyone` says otherwise. A template offered to everyone leaves private lists out. Automations are kept only when the caller may manage automations.
POST /api/v2/projects/:id/template.permission: The project must be one the caller can open

body.name: name
body.description: The template's name, at most 255 characters.

body.name: include.tasks
body.description: Keep the tasks.

body.name: include.assignees
body.description: Keep the assignees.

body.name: include.dates
body.description: Keep the dates, kept as distances from the project's start.

body.name: include.automations
body.description: Keep the automations.

body.name: description
body.description: Up to 2000 characters.

body.name: everyone
body.description: Offer the template to everyone who can create projects. Defaults to `true` unless the project holds a private list.

responseFields.name: template
responseFields.description: The saved template.

responseFields.name: notes
responseFields.description: What was left out or changed, each with a `code` and a `count` or a `name`: `tasks_left_out`, `private_lists_left`, `automations_skipped`, `subfolder_moved_to_top`.

errors.400: The body is missing `name` or `include`, carries another key, has a value of the wrong type, or the project is a personal list; the project holds more than 2000 tasks and `include.tasks` is `true`; or the workspace already holds 100 templates.
errors.404: The project does not exist, is in the trash, or the caller cannot open it.

GET /api/v2/projects/templates.title: List project templates
GET /api/v2/projects/templates.summary: Lists the project templates the caller may use, by name.
description: Owners and admins see every template. Anyone else sees the templates offered to everyone and the ones they saved.
responseNotes: `data` is the template as the caller may see it; `canManage` says whether the caller may change or delete it.
GET /api/v2/projects/templates.paging: None. A workspace holds at most 100 templates.

POST /api/v2/projects/templates/:id/use.title: Create a project from a template
POST /api/v2/projects/templates/:id/use.summary: Creates a project from a template, with its folders, lists and, when asked, its tasks.
description: The caller becomes a member of the new project. People who have left the workspace, and statuses and custom fields that no longer exist, are dropped. Dates are laid out from `startDate`; without it the project and its tasks have no dates.
The answer is the one of [Duplicate a project](#duplicate-a-project).

body.name: name
body.description: The project's name, at most 255 characters.

body.name: include.tasks
body.description: Use the tasks.

body.name: include.assignees
body.description: Use the assignees.

body.name: include.dates
body.description: Use the dates, kept as distances from the project's start.

body.name: include.automations
body.description: Use the automations.

body.name: code
body.description: The project key, letters and digits, at most 10. It must not be taken. Defaults to a generated key.

body.name: isPrivate
body.description: Make the project private. Defaults to the template's own setting.

body.name: startDate
body.description: The project's first day.

responseNotes: `data` has the fields described under [Duplicate a project](#duplicate-a-project).

errors.400: The body is missing `name` or `include`, carries another key, has a value of the wrong type, or `code` is already taken.
errors.404: The template does not exist, or is not one the caller may use.

PATCH /api/v2/projects/templates/:id.title: Change a project template
PATCH /api/v2/projects/templates/:id.summary: Changes a template's name, description or whether it is offered to everyone.
description: A template that holds a private list cannot be offered to everyone. Offering a template to everyone is for the person who saved it; owners and admins may also do it for one saved from a public project.
PATCH /api/v2/projects/templates/:id.permission: The person who saved the template, an owner or an admin

body.name: name
body.description: At most 255 characters.

body.name: description
body.description: Up to 2000 characters.

body.name: everyone
body.description: Offer the template to everyone who can create projects.

bodyNotes: Name at least one key. Any other key is refused.
responseNotes: `data` is the template as the caller may see it; `canManage` says whether the caller may change or delete it.

POST /api/v2/agents/chat/direct.summary: Opens the caller's conversation with an agent.

GET /api/v2/agents/pipeline.summary: Tasks an agent has worked on.

GET /api/v2/agents/release.summary: The release candidate agents have prepared.

POST /api/v2/agents/draft.summary: Drafts a new agent; nothing is stored.

GET /api/v2/agents/budget.summary: This month's agent spend against the budget.

GET /api/v2/agents/routing-policy.summary: Reads which model each kind of task prefers.

GET /api/v2/agents/skills/egress-check.summary: Whether a host is on the workspace's allowed list.

GET /api/v2/agents/memory/project/:proje.summary: Reads what agents remember about a project.

POST /api/v2/agents/memory/project/:proj.summary: Adds something for agents to remember about a project.

GET /api/v2/agents/preferences.summary: Reads the caller's own agent preferences.

PUT /api/v2/agents/preferences.summary: Changes the caller's own agent preferences.

GET /api/v2/agents/reports.summary: The reports delivered to the caller, newest first.

GET /api/v2/agents/runs/summary.summary: The open runs and counts by status.

POST /api/v2/agents/runs.summary: Starts an agent on a task.

GET /api/v2/agents/runs/:id/replay.summary: The prompts and raw responses of a run, for owners and admins.

POST /api/v2/agents/proposals.summary: Files a proposal. Only an agent does, in its own name.

GET /api/v2/agents/account.summary: Reads the caller's linked AI account.

GET /api/v2/agents/project-policy/:proje.summary: Reads a project's policy for agents: whether an agent may close a task (`done`) and how far a connected agent may go on its own (`connected`), with the workspace defaults and the policy in force.

PUT /api/v2/agents/project-policy/:proje.summary: Changes a project's policy for agents. Send `done`, `connected` or both. For an owner or admin who is signed in.

GET /api/v2/agents/project-manager/:proj.summary: Reads whether a project's manager is on, and the findings from its daily look that the caller may open.

PUT /api/v2/agents/project-manager/:proj.summary: Turns a project's manager on or off (`on`). Turning it on looks at the project once straight away. For an owner or admin who is signed in.

GET /api/v2/agents/work-queue/task/:task.summary: What the work queue holds about a task: its items, which connected agent has claimed one, and whether the caller may hand the task over.

POST /api/v2/agents/work-queue/task/:tas.summary: Puts a task in the work queue for a connected agent to pick up, in a project whose manager is on.

POST /api/v2/agents/work-queue/:itemId/t.summary: Takes a work-queue item back from the agent that holds it.

GET /api/v2/agents/work-queue/held.summary: The tasks an agent holds from the work queue right now, among the tasks the caller can open: the task, its project, the agent's name and since when.

GET /api/v2/agents/connected.summary: Each member's connected AI, for a signed-in member. With `taskId`, only the caller's own AI, and only where the caller may hand that task to it.

GET /api/v2/agents/changes.summary: What the caller's own connected agent just changed, for the audit ids in `ids` (at most 50), with whether each can still be undone. For a signed-in person.

GET /api/v2/agents/project-limits/:proje.summary: Reads a project's limits for agents: how many may work at once (`atOnce`) and whether agents are paused there (`paused`), with the defaults and the allowed range.

PUT /api/v2/agents/project-limits/:proje.summary: Changes a project's limits for agents. Send `atOnce`, `paused` or both. Pausing takes held work-queue items back and stops the project's running agent runs. For an owner or admin who is signed in.

GET /api/v2/agents/standing-approvals/:p.summary: The standing approvals ("Always do this") of a project: every one for an owner or admin, the caller's own for a member. For a signed-in person.

DELETE /api/v2/agents/standing-approvals.summary: Removes a standing approval. Its maker, an owner or an admin may remove it. For a signed-in person.

USE /api/v2/goals.summary: Runs before every goal route: reads pass through, and a write (POST, PATCH, PUT or DELETE) made with an agent's token is judged by the rules that hold that agent.

POST /api/v2/agents/:id/schedules.summary: Creates a schedule for an agent.

POST /api/v2/agents/:id/revisions.summary: Creates a revision of an agent.

POST /api/v2/agents/:id/revisions/:n/pro.summary: Makes a revision the live one.

POST /api/v2/agents/:id/revisions/:n/rol.summary: Copies an older revision forward and makes it live.

GET /api/v2/oauth-client-approvals.summary: Lists OAuth clients waiting for approval.

GET /api/v2/oauth-grants.summary: Lists the caller's own OAuth grants.

DELETE /api/v2/oauth-grants/:grantId.summary: Revokes one of the caller's OAuth grants.

POST /api/v2/oauth-grants/:grantId/withd.summary: Withdraws some of the permissions the caller gave a connected app.

GET /api/v2/agent-sessions/endpoints.summary: Reads where outside agents are reached.

PUT /api/v2/agent-sessions/endpoints.summary: Changes where outside agents are reached.

GET /api/v2/agent-sessions.summary: Lists the outside agent sessions of a task.

POST /api/v2/agent-sessions.summary: Hands a task to an outside agent.

POST /api/v2/scim/token.summary: Issues a new SCIM token for the workspace.

GET /api/v2/automations/registry.summary: The triggers and actions an automation can use.

POST /api/v2/automations/compile.summary: Turns a sentence or a rule into a checked automation.

POST /api/v2/automations/draft.summary: Drafts an automation from a sentence.

POST /api/v2/automations/backtest.summary: Shows what a rule would have done on past events.

PATCH /api/v2/automations/:id/enabled.summary: Switches an automation on or off.

POST /api/v2/automations/:id/dry-run.summary: Shows what an automation would do on a task, without doing it.

GET /api/v2/workflows/step-types.summary: The step types a workflow can use.

POST /api/v2/workflows/dry-run.summary: Shows what a workflow would do, without doing it.

PATCH /api/v2/workflows/definitions/:id/.summary: Switches a workflow definition on or off.

GET /api/v2/workflows/approvals.summary: Lists workflow steps waiting for a decision.

GET /api/v2/workflows/runs/:id.summary: Reads a workflow run and its steps.

POST /api/v2/workflows/runs/:id/steps/:s.summary: Hands a step's decision to someone else.

POST /api/v2/tasks/bulk.summary: Runs one change on many tasks at once. The caller must be able to open every task in `taskIds` and hold the permission for the chosen action in their projects, for example `task.task_status` for `bulkUpdateStatus`, `task.task_delete` for `bulkDelete`, `task.task_archive` for `bulkArchive`, `task.task_move` for `bulkMove`. Reads `action` (string, must start with `bulk` and be a known bulk action such as `bulkUpdateStatus`, `bulkUpdatePriority`, `bulkUpdateDueDate`, `bulkUpdateStartDate`, `bulkUpdateDates`, `bulkUpdateAssignee`, `bulkUpdateTags`, `bulkArchive`, `bulkRestore`, `bulkDelete`, `bulkTrash`, `bulkMove`, `bulkConvertToSubTask`, `bulkConvertToTask`, `bulkAddToList`, `bulkDuplicate`) and `taskIds` (list of ids) from the body, plus the fields that action takes, such as `newStatus`, `firebaseObj`, `DueDate`, `startDate`, `employeeId`, `tagId`, `sprintObj`, `projectData`, `parentTaskId`. Answers with `data`: `updated`, `skipped` (task id and reason), `errors`, `totals` (counts of each), and statusText 'Bulk operation completed'. A bad or unknown action answers `status` false with 'Invalid bulk action' or 'Unknown bulk action'. A task or destination the caller cannot open answers 404, a missing permission answers 403.

POST /api/v2/tasks/relations.summary: Links two tasks, unlinks them, or lists a task's links. The caller must be able to open the task, with the `task.task_list` permission in its project. Reads `action` (string: `add`, `remove`, `list` or `openBlockers`) and `companyId` from the body, then `taskId` (id, required), and for `add` and `remove` also `relatedTaskId` (id); for `add` it also reads `type` (one of `blocks`, `blocked_by`, `duplicates`, `duplicated_by`, `relates_to`). Answers with the handler's own envelope: `status`, `statusText` and `data`. For `add` and `remove`, `data` holds `taskId`, `relatedTaskId` and `relations` (only the links the caller can open). For `list`, `data` is the linked tasks, each with `taskId`, `type`, `label`, `createdBy`, `createdAt` and a short `task` summary. For `openBlockers`, `data` is the `blocked_by` links whose blocking task is still open. Failures such as a missing task or two tasks already linked answer `status` false with the error text as statusText. An unknown `action` answers `status` false with 'Invalid relation action'.

POST /api/v2/sprints/burndown.summary: Needs a project the caller can open and a list the caller can see. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the body. Answers with `data`: the sprint's name, state, goal and dates, its totals of tasks, estimate and points, and a `days` series with the ideal line.

POST /api/v2/sprints/hours.summary: Needs a project the caller can open and a list the caller can see. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the body. Answers with `data`: `plannedMinutes`, `loggedMinutes` and `overdueMinutes`, the minutes the sprint is projected to run over its plan.

POST /api/v2/sprints/scrum.summary: Needs write access to the list's project and the permission to create lists there; a person must make the call. Reads `sprintId` (id), `isScrum` (boolean; false turns Scrum off), `goal` (string), `startDate` and `endDate` (dates, both or neither, the end after the start) from the body. A completed sprint cannot be edited, and a running one cannot have Scrum turned off. Answers with `data`: the sprint.

POST /api/v2/sprints/start.summary: Needs write access to the list's project and the permission to create lists there; a person must make the call. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the body. The list must be a sprint with a start and end date, and a project runs one sprint at a time; the tasks in it become the sprint's commitment. Answers with `data`: the started sprint, or a failed status with the reason.

POST /api/v2/sprints/complete.summary: Needs write access to the list's project and the permission to create lists there; a person must make the call. Reads `sprintId` (id) and `incompleteDestination` (`next`, `backlog` or the id of an open sprint of the same project, `next` when left out) from the body. Unfinished tasks move to the destination. Answers with `data`: the completed sprint; a sprint already completed answers success and moves nothing.

GET /api/v2/sprints/complete-preview.summary: Needs a project the caller can open and a list the caller can see. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the query; a list that is not a sprint answers a failed status. Answers with `data`: the sprint's state, commitment, tasks added after the start, and the counts of finished work and of unfinished work with a `list` of it.

POST /api/v2/sprints/backlog.summary: Needs a project the caller can open. Reads `projectId` (id) from the body. Answers with `data`: the project's backlog list, which is made first if it does not exist.

GET /api/v2/sprints/report.summary: Needs a project the caller can open and a list the caller can see. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the query; a list that is not a sprint answers a failed status. Answers with `data`: the sprint's state, goal and dates, and the totals of what was committed, completed and left unfinished, with the tasks added after the start and those moved out.

GET /api/v2/calls/ice-config.summary: The connection settings for a call.

POST /api/v2/calls/notes.summary: Saves the notes of a call.

GET /api/v2/calls/notes.summary: Lists the caller's own call notes.

GET /api/v2/calls/notes/:id.summary: Reads one set of call notes.

PATCH /api/v2/calls/notes/:id.summary: Changes a set of call notes.

GET /api/v2/assignment-rules/project/:pr.summary: Needs a project the caller can open. Answers with `data`: `rules` (`entries` of person and sentence, `fallbackUserId`, `mode`, `onCreate`, `onChange`) and `ai.state`, whether AI is available.

PUT /api/v2/assignment-rules/project/:pr.summary: Needs the permission to change the project's details. Reads `entries` (a list of at most 50 objects with `userId` and `when`, a sentence of at most 300 characters, one per person), `fallbackUserId` (id or empty), `mode` (`suggest` or `apply`, `suggest` when left out), `onCreate` (boolean, true when left out) and `onChange` (boolean, false when left out) from the body; each person must hold a seat and be able to open the project. Answers with `data`: the saved rules.

POST /api/v2/assignment-rules/project/:p.summary: Needs the permission to change the project's details, and AI must be on with a model configured (409 otherwise). Reads `userIds` (a list of 1 to 10 ids) from the body. Answers with `data.drafts`: a suggested rule sentence for each person who can open the project, based on their recent tasks there.

GET /api/v2/assignment-rules/task/:taskI.summary: Needs a task the caller can open (404 otherwise). Answers with `data`: `decision`, the latest open suggestion for the task or `null`, and `pending`, whether one is still being worked out.

POST /api/v2/assignment-rules/task/:task.summary: Needs the permission to change a task's assignee in the task's project. Assigns the suggested person to the task; 409 when the suggestion was already handled, the task already has an assignee, or the person can no longer open it. Answers with `data`: the decision.
Needs the permission to change a task's assignee in the task's project. Marks the suggestion dismissed. Answers with `data`: the decision.
Needs the permission to change a task's assignee in the task's project. Takes back an accepted suggestion. Answers with `data`: the decision.

POST /api/v2/manualLogtime.summary: Adds a manual time entry to a task, or edits one. Needs a task the caller can open. Reads `logTimeDate`, `description`, `startLogTime`, `endLogTime`, `timeDuration` (a string like `HH:MM`), `ticketId`, `projectId`, `isEdit` (a boolean), `dateFormat`, `taskName`, `projectName`, `sprintId` and `timeZone` from the body, all required, plus `timeSheetId` and `previousLoggedTime` when `isEdit` is true. Optional: `userId`, `billable`, `folderId`, `companyOwnerId`. Logging for another person needs the Everyone grant on the user timesheet and the project must be open to the caller, else 403. The person must be a member (400). An entry in an approved, locked period is refused. Answers with `statusText` `Logtime added successfully` and `data`: the saved entry. It also writes task history and a notification.

POST /api/v2/deleteManualLogtime.summary: Deletes a manual time entry. Needs a task the caller can open. Reads `timeSheetId`, `logTimeDate`, `dateFormat`, `startLogTime`, `endLogTime`, `projectId`, `ticketId`, `sprintId`, `taskName` and `projectName` from the body, all required, plus `timeDuration` (minutes), `userId` and `folderId`. Deleting another person's entry needs the Everyone grant on the user timesheet and an open project, else 403. An entry in an approved, locked period is refused. Answers with `statusText` `Logtime deleted successfully`. It also writes task history and a notification.

POST /api/v2/timeTracker/start.summary: Starts a tracker timer on a task. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. The caller can only start a timer for themselves; a `userId` naming someone else answers 403. Reads `description`, `projectId` and `taskId` from the body, all required. A start in an approved, locked period is refused. Answers with `statusText`: the id of the new time entry.

POST /api/v2/timetracker/end.summary: Stops a tracker timer and saves the time. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. The timer must belong to the caller (403 otherwise, 404 if not found). Reads `timeSheetId`, `sprintId`, `projectId`, `taskId`, `taskName`, `projectName`, `companyOwnerId`, `dateFormat`, `timeZone` and `strokes` from the body, all required, plus `considerActionTime` and `actionTime`. A timer that began in an approved, locked period is refused. Answers with `statusText` `Logtime added successfully`. It also writes task history and a notification.

POST /api/v2/timetracker/capture.summary: Stores a tracker screenshot on a running timer and moves its end time forward. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `file`, `path`, `companyId`, `timeSheetId`, `key`, `imageName`, `prevscreenShot`, `screenShotTime`, `memoName` and `strokes` (a JSON string) from a form upload; all are required. `companyId` must match the company header, `timeSheetId` must be a timer of the caller that is still running, and `path` must lie in that timer's own capture folder, or it answers 403 (a path already stored answers 409). The image is read from `file` as a base64 string. Answers with `statusText` `Data Update Succesfully`.

POST /api/v2/timetracker/timelog.summary: Lists the caller's own time entries created in a date range. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Only the caller's own entries are returned; a `userId` naming someone else answers 403. Reads `startDate` and `endDate` (dates, default today) and `type` (the collection name, default the time entries) from the body. Answers with `data`: the matching entries.

GET /api/v2/timetracker/running.summary: Lists the caller's open tracker timers. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `timeZone` (a zone name) from the query. Answers with `data`: up to 20 timers, newest first, each with `timeSheetId`, `taskId`, `taskName`, `sprintId`, `projectId`, `projectName`, `projectColor`, `note`, `startedAt`, `recordedMinutes`, `elapsedSec`, `live`, `overnight` and `suggestedMinutes`.

GET /api/v2/timetracker/can-start.summary: Tells whether the caller may start a timer now. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads nothing. Answers with `statusText` `OK` when it may, or `status` false with `code` `period_locked` when today falls in an approved, locked timesheet period.

POST /api/v2/timetracker/trim.summary: Closes an open timer at a set length. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. The timer must be the caller's own unless the caller is an owner or admin. Reads `timeSheetId` (id) and `minutes` (a whole number from 1 to 1440) from the body, both required. A timer in an approved, locked period is refused. Answers with `statusText` `Timer trimmed.` and `data`: the updated entry. Failures come back with `status` false and a `statusText`.

POST /api/v2/timesheet-approval/submit.summary: Sends a timesheet period in for approval. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. A member submits their own sheet; an owner or admin may pass another member's `userId`, otherwise it is refused. Reads `periodStart` and `periodEnd` (dates, required), `periodType` (string, default `week`), `note` (string) and `userId` from the body. A period that is already approved is refused. It saves the period as submitted with the minutes and entry count logged in it. Answers with `statusText` `Timesheet submitted for approval.` and `data`: the approval record.

GET /api/v2/timesheet-approval/status.summary: Reads the approval record of one timesheet period. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `periodStart` and `periodEnd` (dates, required) and `userId` from the query. Only an owner or admin may read another person's record; for anyone else `userId` is ignored and their own is read. Answers with `data`: the approval record, or null when none exists.

GET /api/v2/timesheet-approval/mine.summary: Lists a person's timesheet submissions, newest period first. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `userId` from the query. Only an owner or admin may read another person's list; for anyone else `userId` is ignored and their own is read. Answers with `data`: the approval records.

GET /api/v2/timesheet-approval/pending.summary: Lists submitted timesheet periods that wait for review. Only an owner or admin may call it; others get `status` false with `statusText` `Only an owner or admin can review timesheets.` Reads nothing. Answers with `data`: the submitted records, oldest first.

GET /api/v2/timesheet-approval/queue.summary: Lists submitted timesheet periods with the context a reviewer needs. Only an owner or admin may call it; others get `status` false. Reads `hoursPerDay` (a number, default 8) from the query. Answers with `data`: the submitted records, oldest first, each with `userName`, `userAvatar`, `totalMinutes`, `entryCount`, `billableMinutes`, `nonBillableMinutes`, `capacityMinutes` and `overMinutes`.

POST /api/v2/timesheet-approval/:id/revi.summary: Approves, rejects or reopens a submitted timesheet period. Only an owner or admin may call it; others get `status` false. Reads `id` (the approval record id) from the path and `action` (`approve`, `reject` or `reopen`) and `reason` (string, needed to reject) from the body. The record must be in a state that allows the action. An owner or admin may approve their own week, and the record is marked as self approved. Answers with `statusText` like `Timesheet approved.` and `data`: the updated record.

POST /api/v2/timesheet-approval/bulk-rev.summary: Approves or rejects several submitted timesheet periods at once. Only an owner or admin has any effect; for others every id is skipped as `not_allowed`. Reads `ids` (a list of record ids, 1 to 100) and `action` (`approve` or `reject`) from the body, both required, plus `reason` (required to reject). Bad input answers 400. Answers with `data`: `results` (one `id` and `outcome` each, `skipped` ones with a `reason`) and `counts` (`approved`, `sent_back`, `skipped`).

GET /api/v2/billing/hourly.summary: A month's billable hours for a project.

GET /api/v2/billing/client-view.summary: What a project's client sees of its billing.

POST /api/v2/billing/client-view/message.summary: Sends a message from the client view.

POST /api/v2/prepare-notification-data.summary: Prepares notification data for the web app.

GET /api/v2/instance/public-config.summary: What the sign-in page needs to know about the instance.

POST /api/v2/csp-report.summary: Receives a browser's content security policy report.

POST /api/v2/support-mail.summary: Sends a message to support from the web app.

DELETE /api/v2/users/sessions/:sessionId.summary: Ends one of the person's sessions.

PUT /api/v2/users/home-cards.summary: Stores the person's home page cards.

GET /api/v2/secrets.summary: Lists the workspace's secrets, by handle only.

GET /api/v2/provider-keys.summary: Lists the workspace's AI provider keys, by handle only.

PUT /api/v2/provider-keys/:provider.summary: Stores a workspace AI provider key.

DELETE /api/v2/provider-keys/:provider.summary: Removes a workspace AI provider key.

GET /api/v2/connectors/slack.summary: Shows the workspace's Slack connector: whether each secret is set and since when, the channel list and, for each allowed channel, whether agents may read it or post to it. Never a secret.

PUT /api/v2/connectors/slack/secrets.summary: Stores the Slack bot token or signing secret in the secrets store, after checking the token with Slack.

POST /api/v2/connectors/slack/channels/r.summary: Reads the Slack channel list again.

PUT /api/v2/connectors/slack/channels.summary: Sets, for each allowed Slack channel, whether agents may read it, propose a message to it, or both.

GET /api/v2/connectors/google/mine.summary: Shows the signed-in member's own Google connections: the account's email, the granted scopes, the dates and the state. Never a token or its handle.

GET /api/v2/connectors/google/members.summary: For an owner or admin: which members hold a Google connection, with its scopes, dates and state. Never the account or a token.

POST /api/v2/connectors/google/:connecto.summary: Starts the signed-in member's Google connection and answers Google's consent address. The state is single-use, lasts ten minutes and belongs to this session.
Completes the connection the same session started: exchanges the code with the PKCE verifier and keeps the tokens in the secrets store.

DELETE /api/v2/connectors/google/:connec.summary: Ends the signed-in member's Google connection: revokes the grant with Google and clears the stored tokens.
For an owner or admin: ends a member's Google connection.

GET /api/v1/connector-oauth/google/callb.summary: Google's redirect after consent. Public: it exchanges nothing and returns the browser to the signed-in page, which completes the connection.

GET /api/v2/ai-switch.summary: Whether AI is on for the workspace.

PUT /api/v2/ai-switch.summary: Turns AI on or off for the workspace.

POST /api/v2/reactions.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace who can read the target. Reads `targetType` (`task` or `comment`), `targetId` (id), `emoji` (string) and `isProjectComment` (boolean) from the body; the caller's own reaction is added, or removed if it is already there. A target the caller cannot read answers 404. Answers with `data.reactions`: the target's reactions.

POST /api/v2/recent-visits.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and it records a visit for that person only. Reads `entityType` (`task`, `project`, `sprint` or `doc`) and `entityId` (id) from the body. Answers with `statusText` `Visit recorded.` and no `data`.

GET /api/v2/recent-visits.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and it lists that person's own visits. Reads `types` (a comma list of `task`, `project`, `sprint` and `doc`, or `all`; tasks only when left out) and `limit` (a number) from the query. Visits to anything deleted or no longer open to the caller drop out. Answers with `data`: the newest visits first.

POST /api/v2/search.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `query` (string) from the body and matches it against task names and keys, project names, comment text and page titles, within the projects, lists and pages the caller can open. Answers with `data`: `tasks`, `projects`, `comments` and `pages`, each limited in number.

POST /api/v2/epics/assign.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the projects of both the task and the epic. Reads `taskId` (id) and `epicId` (id, or empty or null to take the task out) from the body; a task the caller cannot open, or an epic that does not exist, answers a failed status. Answers with `data`: `taskId` and `epicId`.

POST /api/v2/epics/:id/recount.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the epic's project. Counts the epic's tasks again and answers with `data`: the epic with `taskCount` and `completedCount`, counted for tasks the caller can open.

POST /api/v2/epics.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the project named by `projectId`. Reads `name` (string, required), `projectId` (id, required), `description`, `color`, `priority`, `ownerUserId` (strings), `startDate` and `dueDate` from the body; a failed check answers a failed status with the reason. Answers with `data`: the new epic.

GET /api/v2/epics.summary: Needs a project the caller can open, named by the query field `projectId` (id). Answers with `data`: the project's epics, oldest first, with `taskCount` and `completedCount` counted over the tasks the caller can open.

PUT /api/v2/epics/:id.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the epic's project. Reads `name`, `color`, `description`, `status`, `priority`, `ownerUserId`, `startDate` and `dueDate` from the body and changes the ones sent; a body with none of them answers a failed status. Answers with `data`: the epic as it is now.

DELETE /api/v2/epics/:id.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the epic's project. The epic is marked deleted and its tasks are unlinked from it. Answers with `statusText` `Epic deleted.` and no `data`.

GET /api/v2/exports/:id/download.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, for an export the caller started; a workspace export also needs the owner or admin role. Answers with the file once the export has finished, and 404 `Export not ready.` before that.

GET /api/v2/exports.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and it lists only the caller's own exports (a `uid` of someone else answers 403). Answers with `data`: up to 20 exports, newest first, each with `type`, `format`, `status`, `fileName`, `total`, `processed`, `error` and `createdAt`.

POST /api/v2/exports/workspace.summary: Owners and admins only. Reads `format` (`csv` or `xlsx`, `xlsx` when left out) from the body. The export runs in the background. Answers with `data`: the job's `_id`, `type`, `format`, `status`, `fileName` and `createdAt`.

POST /api/v2/exports.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace who can list the project's tasks (404 otherwise). Reads `format` (`csv` or `xlsx`), `projectId` (id), `sprintId` (id, optional) and `projectName` (string) from the body. The export runs in the background. Answers with `data`: the job.

GET /api/v2/api-tokens/needing-expiry.summary: Owners and admins only, and not with an API token (403). Answers with `data`: tokens in the workspace that have no expiry date, and the token `policy`; an empty list while the strict token policy is off.

GET /api/v2/api-tokens/step-credentials.summary: Any member of the workspace, and not with an API token (403). Answers with `data`: the live step credentials, owners and admins seeing all of them and others the ones they started, and `policy`; an empty list while step credentials are off.

GET /api/v2/api-tokens/:id/logs.summary: Only the person who owns the token; any other id answers `Token not found.`. Answers with `data`: the latest 50 calls made with the token, newest first.

POST /api/v2/api-tokens/mcp.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace, and not with an API token (403). Reads `name` (string), `mode` and `provider` (strings), `projectIds` (id list), `expiresInDays` (number), `label` (string), `scopes` and `grants` (lists) from the body; the account `mode` must be one the workspace allows. Answers with `data`: the token, shown once, and the address of the MCP server.

POST /api/v2/api-tokens/:id/renew.summary: Only the person who owns the token, and not with an API token (403). A token that was revoked cannot be renewed. Answers with `data`: the token with a new secret, shown once, and a new end date.

GET /api/v2/api-tokens/ai-connection.summary: Whether the signed-in person's own AI app has connected to this workspace, when it last called, and which groups of tools this server offers it. Never a token or an app's name.

GET /api/v2/api-tokens.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and it lists only that person's own tokens. Answers with `data` (each token's name, prefix, scopes, state and dates, never the secret) and `policy`.

POST /api/v2/api-tokens.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, for the caller's own token. Reads `name` (string), `scopes` (list from the scopes the server offers) and `expiresInDays` (number) from the body. Answers with `data`: the token with its secret, shown once.

PUT /api/v2/api-tokens/:id.summary: Only the person who owns the token. Reads `name` (string) and `active` (boolean) from the body and changes the ones sent; a body with neither answers `Nothing to update.`. Answers with `data`: the token.

DELETE /api/v2/api-tokens/:id.summary: Only the person who owns the token; any other id answers `Token not found.`. Removes the token and its activity log. Answers with `statusText` `Token deleted.` and no `data`.

GET /api/v2/pages/ai-status.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Answers with `data.configured`: whether an AI provider is set up for writing pages.

POST /api/v2/pages/ai.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `action`, `title`, `instruction` and `currentText` (strings) and `pageId` (id of a page the caller may read, whose title and text fill in what is left out) from the body. Answers with `data`: the composed text, or a failed status with the reason, and `isNotAi` when no AI is set up.

GET /api/v2/pages/:id/comments.summary: Any signed-in member who may read the page. Answers with `data`: the page's comments, oldest first, up to 500, with `limit` and `atLimit`.

POST /api/v2/pages/:id/comments.summary: Any signed-in member who may read the page. Reads `message` (string), `blockId` (string), `parentId` (id of a comment to reply under) and an attached file as `mediaURL`, `mediaOriginalName` and `mediaSize` from the body. A page holds at most 500 comments (409). Answers with `data`: the comment.

PUT /api/v2/pages/:id/comments/:commentI.summary: Any signed-in member who may read the page; a thread that has an assignee can be resolved only by the assignee, the person who assigned it or an admin, and a reply cannot be resolved (400). Reads `resolved` (boolean, true when left out; false reopens the thread) from the body. Answers with `data`: the comment.
Only the comment's author, who must be able to read the page (403 for anyone else). Reads `message` (string) from the body. Answers with `data`: the comment as it is now.

DELETE /api/v2/pages/:id/comments/:comme.summary: The comment's author or an admin, who must be able to read the page. A thread is deleted with its replies. Answers with `data._id`: the id of the comment.

GET /api/v2/pages/:id/shares.summary: Only the page's author, or an owner or admin who can open it (403 for anyone else). Answers with `data`: `people`, each with `userId`, `role`, `by`, `at` and `active`, and `limit`.

PUT /api/v2/pages/:id/shares/:userId.summary: Only the page's author, or an owner or admin who can open it. Reads `role` (`viewer` or `editor`, `viewer` when left out) from the body; the person must be an active member of the workspace, and a page can be shared with a limited number of people (400 otherwise). Answers with `data`: the list of people the page is shared with.

DELETE /api/v2/pages/:id/shares/:userId.summary: Only the page's author, or an owner or admin who can open it. Answers with `data`: the list of people the page is still shared with.

PUT /api/v2/pages/:id/review.summary: Needs edit rights on the page, and a share by name as editor is not enough. Reads `nextReviewDate` (a date, three months ahead when left out) from the body, marks the page as a wiki page reviewed now by the caller, and answers with `data`: the page.

PUT /api/v2/pages/:id/approve.summary: Needs edit rights on the page, and a share by name as editor is not enough; a person must make the call. Only a page an agent drafted can be approved, else a failed status. Answers with `data`: the page.

POST /api/v2/pages/:id/images.summary: Needs edit rights on the page. Takes a multipart body with the image as `file`. Answers with `data.key`: the key to put in the page's image block.

GET /api/v2/trash.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `kind` (`projects`, `folders`, `lists`, `tasks` or `docs`, `projects` when left out) from the query. Lists only what the caller could open. Answers with `data`: the trashed items, each with a `title`, a `code` and a `projectId`.

PUT /api/v2/trash/:kind/:id/restore.summary: Needs what deleting that kind needed, in the project the item belongs to; a person must make the call; a doc is judged by the doc rules. The path `kind` is `projects`, `folders`, `lists`, `tasks` or `docs`, and `id` an id. Projects and lists come back together with their tasks. Answers with `data`: the `kind` and `id`.

DELETE /api/v2/sample-data.summary: Removes the sample data a new workspace starts with.

GET /api/v2/forms/fields.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Answers with `data`: the questions a form can ask, as `groups`, the `widgets`, `spans`, `gridColumns` and the task fields a question can be mapped to.

POST /api/v2/forms/:id/publish.summary: Needs edit rights on the form's project (403 without them, 404 when the project cannot be seen). Reads `publish` (boolean, true when left out; false takes the form offline) from the body. A form that fails the checks for going live answers a failed status with the reason. Answers with `data`: `state` and, when live, `token` and `url`.

GET /api/v2/forms/:id/submissions.summary: Needs edit rights on the form's project, because submissions hold the submitters' answers. Reads `q` (string, up to 120 characters, matched against every answer), `page` and `limit` (numbers, 10 per page by default and at most 100) and `all` (`1` returns up to 5000 rows for an export) from the query. Answers with `data`: `submissions`, `total`, `page`, `pages` and `truncated`.

GET /api/v2/forms/:id.summary: Needs a project the caller can open; otherwise 404 `Form not found.`. Answers with `data`: the form with its questions, and its public `url` while it is live.

PUT /api/v2/forms/:id.summary: Needs edit rights on the form's project. Reads `title`, `description`, `successMessage` (strings), `sprintId` (id), `questions` (list), `defaults` (object) and `state` from the body and changes the ones sent; a failed check answers a failed status with the reason. Answers with `data`: the form as it is now.

DELETE /api/v2/forms/:id.summary: Needs edit rights on the form's project. A form that is published answers a failed status, and must be taken offline first. The form is marked deleted and the tasks it filed are kept. Answers with `statusText` `Form deleted.` and no `data`.

GET /api/v2/forms.summary: Needs a project the caller can open, named by the query field `projectId` (id); otherwise 404. Answers with `data`: the project's forms, newest first, each with `title`, `description`, `sprintId`, `state` and `submissionCount`.

POST /api/v2/forms.summary: Needs edit rights on the project named in the body (403 without them, 404 when it cannot be seen). Reads `title` (string, required), `projectId` (id, required), `description` (string) and `sprintId` (id) from the body. The form starts as a draft with no questions. Answers with `data`: the form.

POST /api/v2/public-shares.summary: Creates a public link to a list, a report or a page.

GET /api/v2/public-shares.summary: Lists the public links of something.

PUT /api/v2/public-shares/:id.summary: Switches a public link on or off.

GET /api/v2/who-can-see/:kind/:id.summary: Who can see a project, a list or a page.

POST /api/v2/imports/csv.summary: Imports tasks from a CSV file.

POST /api/v2/imports/clickup/project.summary: Imports a ClickUp export as a new project.

GET /api/v2/custom-fields/formula/scope.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `projectId` (id) and `taskId` (id, used only when the caller can open the task) from the query. Answers with `data`: `names` a formula may use, with the task's values when a task is named, and the lists of `functions` and `rollupFunctions`.

POST /api/v2/custom-fields/formula/valid.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `expression` (string, required), `fieldId`, `fieldTitle`, `projectId` (ids and string) and `sample` (an object of values to try it on) from the body. A formula that does not parse or that closes a cycle answers a failed status with a `code`. Answers with `data`: `references`, `functions`, `preview` and `previewError`.

POST /api/v2/custom-fields/compute.summary: Needs the permission to change a task's custom field. Reads `taskIds` (a list of 1 to 200 ids) and `scope` (`sprint` or left out) from the body; only tasks the caller can open are computed. Answers with `data`: `updated`, the computed `values` and `errors`.

POST /api/v2/custom-fields/:fieldId/ai/p.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace who can edit that field on the task; a task they cannot edit it on comes back with a `reason` instead. Reads `taskIds` (a list of 1 to 5 ids) from the body. Nothing is written. Answers with `data.proposals`: for each task, a `proposalId`, the proposed `text` and `fieldValue`.

POST /api/v2/custom-fields/:fieldId/ai/a.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace who can edit that field on the task. Reads `proposalIds` (a list of up to 5 ids from a preview the same person made) from the body; an expired one is refused. Answers with `data`: `applied` (task ids) and `refused` (with a reason each).

POST /api/v2/custom-fields/:fieldId/ai/j.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace who can edit that field on the tasks. Reads `taskIds` (a list of ids, up to the workspace's bulk limit) and `proposalIds` (a list of up to 5 ids) from the body. The fill runs in the background. Answers with `data`: the job.

GET /api/v2/custom-fields/ai/jobs/:jobId.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace, and only for a job that person started; any other id answers 404 `Job not found.`. Answers with `data`: the job and its progress.

GET /api/v2/task-templates.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `projectId` (id, optional) from the query: with it, the workspace's templates and that project's, for a project the caller can open; without it, the workspace's templates and those of every project the caller can open. Answers with `data`, sorted by name, each with `name`, `scope`, `projectId`, `isDefault`, `canManage` and a count of what it carries.

POST /api/v2/task-templates.summary: Allowed for owners and admins when `scope` is `workspace`, and otherwise for those who can create tasks in the task's project. Reads `name` (string, required), `scope` (`project` or `workspace`, `project` when left out), `taskId` (id of the task to copy from, required) and `include` (an object of booleans, where `false` leaves a part out) from the body. Answers with `data`: the template.

PUT /api/v2/task-templates/default.summary: Needs the permission to change the project's details. Reads `projectId` (id, required) and `templateId` (id, or empty to clear the default) from the body; the template must be a workspace one or that project's. Answers with `statusText` saying whether a default was set or cleared.

POST /api/v2/task-templates/:id/apply.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the task's project; fields the caller's role may not change are skipped and named. Reads `taskId` (id, required), `overwrite` and `preview` (booleans) from the body; with `preview` true nothing is written. Answers with `data`: `applied`, `conflicts`, `skipped`, `checklistAdded` and `subtasksCreated`.

PATCH /api/v2/task-templates/:id.summary: Allowed for owners and admins on a workspace template, and for those who can create tasks in the project on a project template. Reads `name` (string, required) from the body. Answers with `statusText` `Template renamed.` and no `data`.

DELETE /api/v2/task-templates/:id.summary: Allowed for owners and admins on a workspace template, and for those who can create tasks in the project on a project template. The template is marked deleted and is no longer any project's default. Answers with `statusText` `Template deleted.` and no `data`.

GET /api/v2/view-templates.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Answers with `data`, sorted by name, each template with `name`, `viewType` and `canManage`, which is true for owners and admins.

POST /api/v2/view-templates.summary: Needs the permission to change the project's views. Reads `projectId` (id), `viewId` (string) and `name` (string) from the body, and keeps the setup of that view as a template; a workspace holds a limited number. Answers with `data`: the template.

PATCH /api/v2/view-templates/:id.summary: Owners and admins only. Reads `name` (string, required) from the body. Answers with `data`: the renamed template.

DELETE /api/v2/view-templates/:id.summary: Owners and admins only. The template is marked deleted. Answers with `statusText` `Template deleted.` and no `data`.

POST /api/v2/invoices/draft-from-milesto.summary: Drafts an invoice from a milestone.

POST /api/v2/invoices/draft-from-month.summary: Drafts an invoice from a month of logged time.

GET /api/v2/changelog.summary: The product changelog shown in the web app.

GET /api/v1/task/:id.summary: Reads one task by its id.

GET /api/v1/project/:id.summary: Reads one project by its id.

GET /api/v2/setup/status.summary: Whether the instance has been set up.

GET /api/v2/setup/events/:id.summary: The progress stream of the first-run setup.

PATCH /api/tasks/.summary: Changes one task with an older style call that only knows three actions. The caller must be able to open the task and hold the matching task permission in its project: `task.task_status` for `updateStatus`, `task.task_priority` for `updatePriority`, `task.task_name_edit` for `updateTaskName`. Reads `action` (string, one of those three, any other value is refused with 400) from the body, plus the fields of that action: `newStatus`, `prevStatus` (with `taskId`), `task`, `projectData`, `isUpdateTask` for a status change; `firebaseObj` (`Task_Priority`), `taskData`, `priorityObj` (with `taskId`), `projectData` for a priority change; `firebaseObj` (`TaskName`), `taskData`, `obj`, `projectData` for a rename. The acting user is taken from the session, not the body. Answers with `data`: the result of the action, and statusText 'Task updated successfully.'. A task the caller cannot open answers 404 and a missing task permission answers 403; other failures answer `status` false with the error text.

PATCH /api/v1/importTasks.summary: Creates many tasks in one list from imported rows. The caller needs `task.task_create` in the project named by `projectData`, and must be able to see the target list (a private list is only for its people and the admins). AI agent accounts are refused. Reads `tasks` (list of task rows), `projectData` (object with `_id` and `CompanyId`), `sprint` (object with `id`, the list to import into), `statusArray` (list of statuses with `name`, `key`, `type`), `indexObj`, `eventId` (a string used to report progress) and `userData` from the body. The list must belong to the project, else it answers 404 'Project or sprint not found.'. A missing permission answers 403 'You do not have permission to import tasks into this project.'. On success answers with `data`: `createdTasks`, `customFields`, `adjusted`, `droppedFieldValues`, and statusText 'Task updated successfully.'.

POST /api/v1/tabSyncTask.summary: Returns the tasks of one list that changed since the person left the browser tab, so the board or table can refresh. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and the rows are limited to tasks the caller may see. Reads `pid` (project id, required), `sprintId` (list id, required), `istableTask` (boolean, required, true for table view and false for board view), `tabLeaveTime` (a time in milliseconds), `item` (the group being refreshed, with `indexName` and `mongoConditions` or `conditions`), `indexName`, `sortKey` (like 'field:1'), `showAllTasks`, `userId` and `parentId` (to read sub tasks of one parent) from the body. Answers with the raw list of matching rows, not wrapped in `data`; for board view it is one object holding `result` (changed tasks) and `count`. A missing required field or a refused query answers 400 with `message`.

POST /api/v1/task/filter/create.summary: Saves a task filter for the caller. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and the filter always belongs to the caller. Reads the filter fields from the body, for example `name`, `filters`, `sortByField`, `sortByOrder`; any `_id` is dropped and `userId` and `companyId` are set by the server. A `userId` naming someone else answers 403 'A saved filter can only be created for yourself.'. Answers with `status` true and `data`: the saved filter. A failure answers 500 with statusText.

GET /api/v1/task/filter/:userId.summary: Lists the saved task filters of the caller. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, but only for themselves. Reads `userId` (id) from the path; if it is not the caller's own id it answers 403 'You can only read your own saved filters.'. Answers with `status` true and `data`: the caller's saved filters of kind `taskFilter` for `projectTask`, or an empty list. A failure answers 500 with statusText.

PUT /api/v1/task/filter/update.summary: Changes one saved task filter of the caller. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and it can only touch filters the caller owns. The body is a list of two items: first `{ _id }` (the filter id, required, 24 character id), then `{ $set }` holding any of `name`, `filters`, `sortByField`, `sortByOrder` (other fields are ignored). Reads `projectId` from the query only to write a history line. A bad id or an empty update answers 400, a filter that is not found for the caller answers 404 'Saved filter not found.'. On success answers `status` true with no `data`.

DELETE /api/v1/task/filter/delete/:cid/:.summary: Deletes one saved task filter of the caller. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and it can only remove filters the caller owns. Reads `cid` (company id, must equal the workspace in the `companyid` header, else 403) and `id` (filter id) from the path, and `projectId` from the query only to write a history line. A bad id answers 400, a filter that is not found for the caller answers 404 'Saved filter not found.'. On success answers `status` true with no `data`.

POST /api/v1/task/find.summary: Runs a read only search over tasks using a query pipeline and returns the matching tasks. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and the server first narrows the rows to tasks the caller may see. Reads `findQuery` (a list of query stages, or one stage, required), `replaceUndefined` (boolean) and `inList` (a list id, so that tasks added to that list as an extra list are included) from the body. Answers with the raw list of matching rows, not wrapped in `data`. A missing query answers 400 'Query is required.', a stage that is not allowed answers 400 'Query refused' with `message` and `stage`, and other failures answer 500.

PUT /api/v1/task.summary: Moves every task of one project between active, closed, deleted and restored states, to follow a change of the project itself. AI agent accounts are refused. The caller must be a member of the workspace and, unless owner or admin, able to open the project, and must hold the permission for the change: `project.project_close` for 0 to 8, `project.project_delete` for 0 to 7 or 0 to 1, `project.project_list` for 7 to 0 or 8 to 0.
