Reads `key` (string, must be `updateMany`), `firstParameter` (object with `ProjectID` or `objId.ProjectID`, and `deletedStatusKey` as the current state number) and `secondParameter` (object `{ $set: { deletedStatusKey } }` with the new state number), all required; any other body key is refused. Answers with `data`: the update result (`matchedCount`, `modifiedCount`), and statusText 'Tasks updated successfully.'. A refused request answers 403 with statusText 'Forbidden' and a `message`; a missing field answers 400.

POST /api/v1/sprint.summary: Creates a list (sprint) in a project, or a chat channel. The caller needs `project.project_sprint_create` in the project (chat channels are judged by chat access instead), and any person named as a member of a channel must be a member of the workspace. AI agent accounts are refused. Reads `projectId` (id), `sprintName` (string), `folder` (object with `folderId`, the folder to put it in, which must be a live folder of the project), `private` (boolean), `icon`, `mainChat` (boolean, for a chat channel), `AssigneeUserId` and `sendMessage` (channels only), `isPreCompany`, `from` and `taskSprintObj` from the body. The acting user is taken from the session. Answers with `data`: the new list, and statusText 'List added successfully'. It answers `status` false with 'Upgrade your plan' (and `isUpgrade` true) when the plan's list limit is reached, or 'Channels creation limits have been exceeded' for channels. Other failures answer `status` false with the error text.

PATCH /api/v1/sprint/:id.summary: Renames, updates or deletes one list (sprint) or chat channel, depending on `type`. The caller must be able to open the list and write in its project, and needs the permission that matches the change: `project.project_sprint_name_edit` for a rename, `project.sprint_delete` for `deleteChannel`, and for `updateSprint` the restore, delete or archive key for the new `deletedStatusKey`, or the edit or share keys when it moves a list or changes who may see it. AI agent accounts are refused. Reads `id` (list id) from the path and `type` (string, one of `editSprintName`, `updateSprint`, `deleteChannel`, required) from the body. For `editSprintName` it reads `sprintName` (string, 1 to 50 characters) and `projectId`. For `updateSprint` it reads `updateObject`, which may only `$set` `deletedStatusKey`, `private`, `AssigneeUserId`, `folderId`, `folderName`, or `$addToSet` or `$pull` one member or watcher. A list that is running a Scrum sprint cannot be archived. For `deleteChannel` it reads `companyId`. Answers with `data`: the updated list, and statusText 'Sprint_updated_successfully' (or 'Sprint_deleted_successfully' for a delete). A missing `type` answers `status` false with 'type not found', an unknown `type` answers 400 'Invalid type', a list that is not found answers `status` false with 'Sprint not found'.

POST /api/v1/folder.summary: Creates a folder in a project, or a category in a chat space. The caller needs `project.project_folder_create` in the project (chat categories are judged by chat access instead). AI agent accounts are refused. Reads `projectId` (id), `folderName` (string), `parentFolderId` (id of a live folder of the same project, optional, folders nest one level) and `mainChat` (boolean) from the body. The acting user is taken from the session. Answers with `data`: the new folder, and statusText 'Folder added successfully'. A bad parent answers 400 with the reason, other failures answer `status` false with the error text.

PATCH /api/v1/folder/:id.summary: Renames, moves, archives, deletes or restores one folder, depending on `type`. The caller must be able to open the folder's project and needs the permission for the change: `project.project_folder_name_edit` for a rename, that key or `project.project_folder_create` for a move, `project.folder_archive`, `project.folder_delete` or `project.folder_restore` for the matching `deletedStatusKey`. AI agent accounts are refused. Reads `id` (folder id) from the path and `type` (string, one of `editFolderName`, `updateFolder`, `moveFolder`, required) from the body. For `editFolderName` it reads `folderName` and `projectId`, and also renames the folder copy kept on its tasks. For `moveFolder` it reads `parentFolderId` (an id, or null for the top level; required). For `updateFolder` it reads `updateObject`, which may only be `{ $set: { deletedStatusKey } }` with 0, 1 or 2, and it carries sub folders and their tasks along. Answers with `data`: the folder, and statusText 'Folder renamed successfully', 'Folder moved successfully' or 'Folder updated successfully' (`updateFolder` also returns `subfolders`). A missing `type` answers `status` false with 'type not found', an unknown `type` answers 400 'Invalid type', a folder that is not found answers `status` false with 'Folder not found'.

GET /api/v1/agile/burndown.summary: Gives the burndown of one list (sprint): how much work is left each day against an ideal line. The caller must be able to open the sprint's project and the sprint itself (a private sprint is only for its people and the admins). Reads `sprintId` (id, required) from the query. Answers with `data`: `sprintName`, `isScrum`, `state`, `goal`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `totalCount`, `totalEstimate`, `totalPoints` and `days` (each with `date`, `remainingCount`, `remainingEstimate`, `remainingPoints`, `ideal`, `idealPoints`), and statusText 'Burndown computed.'. A list with no tasks answers `data` with an empty `days`. A bad id answers `status` false with 'companyId and a valid sprintId are required.', a missing sprint answers `status` false with 'Sprint not found.'.

GET /api/v1/agile/velocity.summary: Gives the velocity of a project: points promised against points finished across its latest closed Scrum sprints, with a rolling average of three. The caller must be able to open the project, and private sprints they are not on are left out unless they are owner or admin. Reads `projectId` (id, required) and `limit` (a number, between 1 and 50, default 10) from the query. Answers with `data`: `sprints` (each with `sprintId`, `name`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `committed`, `completed`, `completedHuman`, `completedAgent`, `unchecked`, `byPattern`, `rollingAvg`) and `skipped` (closed sprints without a start snapshot), and statusText 'Velocity computed.' or 'No completed sprints yet.'. A bad id answers `status` false with 'companyId and a valid projectId are required.'.

GET /api/v1/agile/cfd.summary: Gives the cumulative flow of a project: how many tasks sit in each status group on each day. The caller must be able to open the project, and tasks in private sprints they cannot see are left out. Reads `projectId` (id, required), `from` and `to` (dates, optional, default is the last 30 days, at most 120 days) from the query. Answers with `data`: `days`, each with `date` and the counts `open`, `inprogress`, `onhold`, `close`, and statusText 'CFD computed.' or 'No tasks yet.'. A bad id answers `status` false with 'companyId and a valid projectId are required.'.

GET /api/v1/agile/sprint-insights.summary: Gives extra facts for one list (sprint): which tasks are blocked and for how long, and which tasks were added after the sprint started. The caller must be able to open the sprint's project and the sprint itself. Reads `sprintId` (id, required) from the query. Answers with `data`: `sprintId`, `sprintName`, `projectId`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `blockers` (with `blockedDays` and `since`), `scopeAdds` (with `action`, `by`, `at`, `done`), `tasks` (each with `done`, `blocked`, `committed`) and `hasCommitment`, and statusText 'Sprint insights computed.'. A bad id answers `status` false with 'companyId and a valid sprintId are required.', a missing sprint answers `status` false with 'Sprint not found.'.

GET /api/v1/agile/milestones.summary: Lists the dated milestones of a project, or of every project the caller can open, with how each one is doing. The caller only sees projects they can open, and tasks in private sprints they cannot see are not counted. Reads `projectId` (id, optional) from the query; a value that is not an id answers `status` false. Answers with `data`: `milestones` (each with `milestoneId`, `name`, `projectId`, `projectName`, `baseline`, `target`, `targetField`, `slipDays`, `tasks`, `doneTasks`, `overdueTasks`, `openTasks`, `signedOff`, `state` of `done`, `missed`, `at-risk` or `on-track`, `lastMove`, `moveCount`) and `totals` (`total`, `onTrack`, `atRisk`, `missed`, `done`), and statusText 'Milestones computed.'. With no visible project it answers statusText 'No projects.' and empty lists.

GET /api/v1/agile/provenance.summary: Shows who finished the work in a list (sprint) or a project, people or AI agents, with a cost split. The caller must be able to open the project, and for a sprint also the sprint itself. Reads `sprintId` (id) or `projectId` (id) from the query, one of them is required. Answers with `data`: `sprint` (`id` and `name`, or null), `projectId`, the completion split fields, and `margin` (with `currencySymbol`), and statusText 'Provenance computed.'. A missing or bad id answers `status` false with 'companyId and a valid sprintId or projectId are required.', a missing sprint answers `status` false with 'Sprint not found.'.

POST /api/v1/recurring-tasks.summary: Creates a repeating task rule for a project. The caller needs `task.task_create` in the project named by `projectData`. Reads `name` (string, required), `taskName` (string, required), `projectData` (object with `_id` required, plus `CompanyId`, `ProjectCode`, `ProjectName`), `freq` (required, `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`), `interval` (a number), `byweekday` (list of numbers 0 to 6), `monthday` (a number), `runHour` (a number, default 9), `skipIfOpen` (boolean), `missedPolicy` (`skip`, `create` or `roll`), `until` (a date), `sprintId` or `sprintArray`, `assignees` (list of user ids), `taskType`, `taskTypeKey`, `priority`, `points`, `rawDescription`, `descriptionBlock` and `userData` from the body. A missing required field answers `status` false with 'Missing required fields (name, taskName, projectData, freq)'. Answers with `data`: the saved rule, and statusText 'Recurring task created'. A description that is too long answers 400.

GET /api/v1/recurring-tasks/task/:taskId.summary: Reads the repeat rule of one task. The caller must be able to open the task's project. Reads `taskId` (id) from the path. Answers with `status` true and `data`: the rule, or null when the task does not repeat. A bad id answers 400 'A valid task id is required.', a task that is not found answers 404 'Task not found.'.

PUT /api/v1/recurring-tasks/task/:taskId.summary: Makes a task repeat, or changes how it repeats. The caller needs `task.task_due_date` and `task.task_create` in the task's project. Reads `taskId` (id) from the path and `freq` (required, `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`), `interval` (whole number from 1 up), `byweekday` (list of days 0 to 6), `monthday` (1 to 31), `runHour` (0 to 23), `until` (a date), `maxRuns` (whole number) and `missedPolicy` (`skip`, `create` or `roll`) from the body. The acting user comes from the session. Answers with `data`: the rule, and statusText 'Repeat set' for a new rule or 'Repeat updated' for an existing one. A bad schedule or id answers 400 with the reason, a task that is not found answers 404 'Task not found.'.

DELETE /api/v1/recurring-tasks/task/:tas.summary: Stops a task from repeating by removing its repeat rule. The caller needs `task.task_due_date` in the task's project. Reads `taskId` (id) from the path. Answers with `status` true and statusText 'Repeat removed', also when the task had no rule. A bad id answers 400, a task that is not found answers 404 'Task not found.'.

PATCH /api/v1/recurring-tasks/:id.summary: Changes a repeat rule. The caller must be able to write in the rule's project (no task permission key is checked here). Reads `id` (rule id) from the path and any of `name`, `enabled`, `freq`, `interval`, `byweekday`, `monthday`, `runHour`, `skipIfOpen`, `missedPolicy` and `until` from the body; when the schedule fields change the next run time is worked out again. Answers with `status` true and statusText 'Updated'. A failure answers `status` false with the error text.

DELETE /api/v1/recurring-tasks/:id.summary: Deletes a repeat rule by switching it off and marking it deleted. The caller must be able to write in the rule's project (no task permission key is checked here). Reads `id` (rule id) from the path. Answers with `status` true and statusText 'Deleted'. A failure answers `status` false with the error text.

POST /api/v1/recurring-tasks/:id/run-now.summary: Makes one task from a repeat rule right now. The caller needs `task.task_create` in the rule's project. Reads `id` (rule id) from the path. Answers with `data`: `id` (the new task id or null) and `skipped` (true when the last task is still open and the rule's policy says not to make another), and statusText 'Task created' or 'Skipped, previous instance still open'. A rule that is not found answers `status` false with 'Definition not found'.

POST /api/v1/recurring-tasks/run-due.summary: Runs every repeat rule of the workspace that is due now. Only an owner or an admin may call it. Reads nothing from the body. Answers with `data`: `processed` (rules looked at) and `created` (tasks made), and statusText 'Processed due recurring tasks'. A failure answers `status` false with the error text.

POST /api/v1/taskIndex.summary: Saves the new place of a task after it is dragged on a board, and changes any field the drag changed. The caller must be able to open the task, with the `task.task_list` permission in its project. Reads from the body, all required: `taskId`, `projectId`, `sprintId`, `taskKey`, `isFirst` (boolean), `isFirstWithRecord` (boolean), `relevantIndex` (a number), `indexName` (one of `groupByStatusIndex`, `groupByPriorityIndex`, `groupByAssigneeIndex`, `groupByDueDateIndex`), `searchKey` (one of `statusKey`, `Task_Priority`, `AssigneeUserId`, `DueDate`), `relevantKey` and `updateData` (object with the changed `statusKey`, `Task_Priority`, `AssigneeUserId`, `DueDate` and so on). The workspace is taken from the header. The work is queued per project and done after the answer, so it answers right away with `status` true and statusText 'Process Is Start For Index'. A missing field answers 400 '<field> is required'.

POST /api/v1/updateTaskIndexOnload.summary: Gives a task a board position when it has none for the chosen grouping, as the board loads. The caller must be able to open the task, with the `task.task_list` permission in its project. Reads `taskUpdate` (required) from the body: an object with `data` (the task id) and `item` (with `indexName`, `searchKey`, `searchValue`). Answers with `status` true and statusText 'Index Update Successfully' when it set a position, or 'No Need To Processs' when the task already had one. A missing `taskUpdate` answers `status` false with 'Task Update Is Required', and a task that is not found answers 404 'Task not found'.

PUT /api/v1/taskPriority.summary: Changes the workspace's list of task priorities. Only an owner or an admin may call it. Reads `key` (string, required, `$push` or `$pull`) and `updateObject` (object, required, holding `settings` with one priority entry) from the body. A missing or invalid value answers 400 with `message`. Answers with the raw update result (not wrapped in `data`), and clears the cached priority list. A failure answers 500 with `message` and `error`.

GET /api/v1/taskPriority.summary: Lists the workspace's task priorities. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads nothing from the body or query; the workspace comes from the `companyid` header. Answers with the raw list of settings documents named for task priorities (not wrapped in `data`), kept in a cache for a week and marked with a `FromCache` header when it came from there. A missing header answers 400, a failure answers 500 with `message`.

GET /api/v1/recurring-tasks/project/:pid.summary: Lists the recurring task rules of one project. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner). Reads `pid` (id) from the path. Answers with `data`: the project's recurring task rules that are not deleted. On an error it answers `status` false with `statusText`.

POST /api/v1/projectSetting/taskType.summary: Moves every task of the old task types in a project over to the new type chosen for each one. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members also need the `project.project_details` permission for that project. Reads `projectId` (id, required), `taskTypeKey` (list, required) and `oldTaskType` (list, required; each item has `key` and `convertType` with `key` and `value`) from the body. Answers `status` true with `statusText`: "TASK UPDATE SUCCESFULLY". A missing field answers `status` false with a `statusText` naming it.

POST /api/v1/projectSetting/taskStatus.summary: Moves every task in the old statuses of a project over to the new status chosen for each one. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members also need the `project.project_details` permission for that project. Reads `projectId` (id, required), `taskStatusKey` (list, required) and `oldTaskStatus` (list, required; each item has `key` and `convertStatus` with `key`, `name` and `type`) from the body. Answers `status` true with `statusText`: "TASK UPDATE SUCCESFULLY". A missing field answers `status` false with a `statusText` naming it.

POST /api/v1/projectSetting/taskStatus/w.summary: Sets or clears the work in progress limit of one status column in a project. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members also need the `project.project_details` permission for that project. Reads `projectId` (id, required), `statusKey` (required) and `wipLimit` (a number) from the body. A value that is empty, zero or below clears the limit, and the limit tops out at 999. Answers with `data`: `statusKey`, `wipLimit`, `taskStatusData`, and `statusText` says the limit was set or cleared. Failures answer `status` false with `statusText` (bad project id, project not found, status not on the project).

POST /api/v1/projectSetting/migrateSprin.summary: Runs a one time migration that turns the sprints and folders stored inside every project and chat of the workspace into their own records. Only the instance owner may call it, or a script that sends the `adminkey` header; an API token is refused. Reads nothing from the body or query. Answers `status` true with `statusText`: "done" once every project was processed.

GET /api/v1/projectSetting/autoArchive/:.summary: Reads the auto archive rule of a project. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner). Reads `pid` (id) from the path. Answers with `data`: `enabled` (true or false) and `afterDays` (days, 1 to 365, default 30). A missing project answers `status` false with `statusText`.

POST /api/v1/projectSetting/autoArchive.summary: Sets the rule that archives finished tasks of a project after some days. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members also need the `project.project_details` permission for that project. Reads `projectId` (id, required), `enabled` (true or false) and `afterDays` (a number, kept between 1 and 365) from the body. Answers with `data`: `enabled` and `afterDays` as saved. A missing project answers `status` false with `statusText`.

POST /api/v1/projectSetting/estimationSc.summary: Sets the story point scale a project offers. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members also need the `project.project_details` permission for that project. Reads `projectId` (id, required) and `scale` (one of fibonacci, linear, tshirt, hours; anything else becomes fibonacci) from the body. Answers with `data`: `estimationScale`. A missing project answers `status` false with `statusText`.

POST /api/v1/createproject.summary: Creates a new project, with its first list, in the workspace. Needs the `project.project_create` permission, and any people named in `AssigneeUserId`, `LeadUserId` or `watchers` must be members. Reads from the body `ProjectName` (required), `ProjectCode` (required), `source` (required), `proposalId` (required when the source is upwork), `projectIcon`, `isPrivateSpace` (true or false), `isTemplate`, `ProjectRequiredComponent` and other project fields. The workspace and creator are set from the session, so a body naming another company is refused with 403. Answers with `data`: the new project, and `statusText`: "createProject added successfully". Failures answer `status` false with `statusText` giving the reason.

GET /api/v1/project-close.summary: Reads the workspace policy for closing inactive projects. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads nothing from the body or query. Answers with `data`: `policy` and `validInactiveMonths`.

PUT /api/v1/project-close.summary: Changes the workspace policy for closing inactive projects. Only an owner or an admin may call it, otherwise it answers 403. Reads `enabled` (true or false) and `inactiveMonths` (a number from the allowed list) from the body, and needs at least one of them. Answers with `data`: `policy` as saved, and `statusText`: "Auto-close settings updated". A bad value answers 400 with `statusText`.

POST /api/v1/project/search.summary: Searches the projects, sprints, folders or archived lists the caller can see. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and results only include projects the caller may open (private ones only if assigned or if their role sees all private projects). Reads `type` (required; one of sprint, folder, projectName, projectFilter, projectFilter_projectName, projectFilter_folder, projectFilter_sprint, showArchiveOnly) from the body, plus `search` (string), `fields` (comma separated string), `query`, `sortByField`, `sortByOrder`, `showArchived`, `skip` and `limit` (numbers). Answers with the list of matches itself (no `data` wrapper), or an empty list if the caller has no active seat. A missing `type` answers 404 with `message`.

PUT /api/v1/project/:id.summary: Updates fields of one project. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members need the permission tied to each field they change (for example the name, dates, status, assignee or description permissions), and `project.project_details` for fields without their own key. Reads `id` (id) from the path and `updateObject` (object, required), `key` (one of $set, $unset, $push, $pull, $addToSet; default $set), `arrayFilters` (list) and `timeZone` (string) from the body. Server owned fields such as the creator, company or counters cannot be changed and answer 400, and moving a project is refused for agent tokens. People named must be members. Answers with the project record. Failures answer 400 with `message` (for example a bad source or proposal id) or 500.

PUT /api/v1/project/:id/view-settings.summary: Saves the settings of one view of a project. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members also need the `project.view_list` or `project.project_details` permission. Reads `id` (id) from the path and `viewId` (string, required) and `settings` (object, required) from the body. Answers with `data`: `viewId` and the cleaned `settings`, and `statusText`: "View saved.". An unknown view or project answers 404.

POST /api/v1/project/:id/views.summary: Adds a new view to a project, copied from an existing view or built from a view template. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members also need the `project.view_list` or `project.project_details` permission. Reads `id` (id) from the path. In the body it reads either `templateId` (with optional `title`, `isPrivate`, `isPin`) or `sourceViewId` (string, required) with `title` (required) and optional `settings` (object). Answers with `data`: the new view (or a prepared private view), `leftOut`, and `statusText`: "View added." A project holds at most 60 views. An unknown view or template answers 404, and a bad body answers 400.

PUT /api/v1/project/allTask/:id.summary: Changes the deleted state of tasks in a project, used when a project is closed, deleted, archived or restored. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members need the `project.project_delete` or `project.project_close` permission, and agent tokens are refused. Reads `id` (id) from the path and `findObject` (required; only `ProjectID` and `deletedStatusKey`) and `updateObject` (required; only `deletedStatusKey`, a whole number) from the body. Answers with `data`: `matched` and `modified`, and `statusText`: "Project tasks updated." Bad input answers 400 with `statusText`.

GET /api/v1/project/sprintFolder/:id.summary: Lists the sprints or folders of a project, or counts them. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner). Reads `id` (id) from the path and `collection` (required; sprints or folders), `count`, `fields` (comma separated string), `skip` and `limit` from the query. Sprints the caller may not see are left out unless the caller is an owner or admin, and removed ones are left out. Answers with the list itself (no `data` wrapper), or a count when `count` is set. A missing or unknown `collection` answers 400 with `message`.

PUT /api/v1/project/sprint/:id.summary: Adds or removes the caller's own favourite star on a list (sprint). Needs access to the sprint and its project, and no extra permission for this own star. Reads `id` (id) from the path and `key` ($addToSet or $pull) and `updateObject` from the body, which must be exactly `{ favouriteTasks: { userId } }` with the caller's own id. Anything else answers 400. Answers with the updated sprint.

POST /api/v1/project/filter/create.summary: Saves a project filter for the caller. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and the filter always belongs to the caller. Reads `name` (string, required, up to 200 characters), `filter` (string, required), `typeFilter` (string, required), `filters` (list), `sortByField` and `sortByOrder` (objects) and `userId` (must be the caller's own) from the body. Answers with `data`: the saved filter, and `statusText`: "Filter saved." A bad field answers 400 with `statusText` and `field`, and another user's id answers 403.

GET /api/v1/project/filter/:userId.summary: Lists the caller's saved project filters. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, but `userId` (id, from the path) must be the caller's own id or it answers 403. Answers with `data`: the caller's saved filters of the project kind.

DELETE /api/v1/project/filter/delete/:ci.summary: Deletes one saved filter of the caller. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, but only the owner of the filter can delete it. Reads `cid` (id, must match the workspace of the request) and `id` (id, the filter) from the path, and an optional `projectId` from the query for the history. Answers `status` true. A wrong company answers 403, a bad id 400, and a filter that is not the caller's or does not exist 404.

PUT /api/v1/project/filter/update.summary: Changes one saved project filter of the caller. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, but only the owner of the filter can change it. Reads `id` (id, required; `_id` also works) and at least one of `name`, `filters` (list), `sortByField`, `sortByOrder` (objects) from the body, and `userId` if sent must be the caller's own. Answers with `data`: the updated filter, and `statusText`: "Filter updated." A bad field answers 400, another user's id 403, and a filter that is not found 404.

POST /api/v1/project/checklist.summary: Adds, changes or removes items of a project's checklist. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members need the `project.project_checklist` permission; adding or removing an assignee on an item can be done with either `project.project_checklist_assign_remove` or `project.project_checklist`. Reads `id` (the project id), `operation` (push, update or delete), `checklistItem` (an item, or a list of item ids for delete) and `key` (name, isChecked, assigneeAdd or assigneeRemove, for update) from the body. An update by name or assignee needs `checklistItem.id`. Answers `status` true. An unknown project answers 404 and a bad `operation` answers 400 with `message`.

POST /api/v1/get-remaining-projects.summary: Fetches the full records of projects from a list of ids. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and ids of projects the caller cannot open are dropped from the list first. Reads `dataIds` (list of project ids, required) from the body. Answers with `data`: the matching projects. An empty or badly formed list, or one with nothing left after dropping, answers 400 with `statusText` and `field`.

POST /api/v1/project/tags.summary: Adds, renames, recolours or removes a tag defined on a project. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner), and owners and admins always pass. Other members need the `task.task_tag` permission. Reads `id` (the project id), `operation` (push, update or delete), `items` (the tag; for update and delete it needs `id`, the tag's `uid`) and `key` (tagName or tagColor, for update) from the body. Answers `status` true. An unknown project answers 404 and a bad `operation` answers 400 with `message`.

GET /api/v1/projectdata/taskData.summary: Reads one task with its project, list, folder and its subtasks. Needs a project the caller can open (a private project only for people assigned to it or roles that see every private project; a personal list only for its owner). The caller must also be able to read the task, or it answers 404. Reads `taskId` (id, required), `projectId` (id, required) and `subTaskLimit` (a number, required) from the query. Answers with the list result itself (no `data` wrapper): the project row with `tasks`, `subtasks` (newest first, up to `subTaskLimit`) and `parentFolder`. A missing or malformed parameter answers 400 with `message`.

POST /api/v1/project/personal.summary: Finds the caller's personal list project, or creates it the first time. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and it only ever returns the caller's own personal project. Reads nothing from the body or query. Answers with `data`: `project` and `sprint` (its first list), and `statusText` is "Personal list created" or "Personal list found". Failures answer 400 with `message`.

POST /api/v1/project/template/custom.summary: Saves a custom project template for the workspace. Only an owner or an admin may call it, otherwise it answers 403. Reads `data` (object, required) from the body; `data.TemplateName` is required, a string of up to 250 characters. Answers with `data`: the saved template, and `statusText`: "Template saved." A bad name answers 400 with `statusText` and `field`.

POST /api/v1/project/template/custom/ai-.summary: Asks the AI to draft task statuses, task types and project statuses for a project template, without saving anything. Only an owner or an admin may call it, otherwise it answers 403. Reads `category` (string, required) and `useCaseDescription` (string) from the body. Answers with `data`: the draft template (`taskStatusData`, `TemplateTaskType`, `projectStatusData`, `finalTemplateTaskStatusData`, `finalProjectStatusData`), matched to the workspace's existing statuses and types. A missing `category` answers 400, and so does an AI that is not set up.

DELETE /api/v1/project/template/custom/:.summary: Deletes one custom project template. Only an owner or an admin may call it, otherwise it answers 403. Reads `id` (id) from the path. Answers `status` true, or `status` false with 404 when nothing was deleted.

GET /api/v1/project/template/custom.summary: Lists the custom project templates of the workspace. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads nothing from the body or query. Answers with `data`: the templates (served from a cache when one is fresh).

POST /api/v3/timeTracker/start.summary: Starts a tracker timer on a task, for the desktop tracker. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. The caller can only start a timer for themselves; a `userId` naming someone else answers 403. Only users marked as tracker users may start one, else it answers `isPermissionDenied`. Reads `description`, `projectId` and `taskId` from the body, all required, plus `considerActionTime` (boolean) and `actionTime` (a Unix time in seconds) to set the start time. A start in an approved, locked period is refused. Answers with `statusText`: the id of the new time entry.

POST /api/v3/timetracker/capture.summary: Stores a tracker screenshot on a running timer and moves its end time forward. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `file`, `path`, `companyId`, `timeSheetId`, `key`, `imageName`, `prevscreenShot`, `screenShotTime`, `memoName` and `strokes` (a JSON string) from a form upload; all are required. `companyId` must match the company header, `timeSheetId` must be a timer of the caller that is still running, and `path` must lie in that timer's own capture folder, or it answers 403 (a path already stored answers 409). The image is the uploaded file. Answers with `statusText` `Data Update Succesfully`.

POST /api/v4/timetracker/capture.summary: Stores a tracker screenshot on a running timer and moves its end time forward, for the desktop tracker. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `file`, `path`, `companyId`, `timeSheetId`, `key`, `imageName`, `prevscreenShot`, `screenShotTime`, `memoName` and `strokes` (a JSON string) from a form upload; all are required. `companyId` must match the company header, `timeSheetId` must be a timer of the caller that is still running, and `path` must lie in that timer's own capture folder, or it answers 403 (a path already stored answers 409). The image is the uploaded file. Only tracker users may use it, else it answers `isPermissionDenied`. It also reads `considerActionTime` and `actionTime` (seconds) to set the end time. Answers with `statusText` `Data Update Succesfully`.

GET /api/v1/estimatedTime/:pid/:tid.summary: Lists the planned time rows for one task. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Callers without the Everyone grant on the workload or project timesheet see only their own rows, and only for projects they can open; a project they cannot open gives an empty list. Reads `pid` (project id) and `tid` (task id) from the path. Answers with the list of rows itself, not wrapped in `data`.

PUT /api/v1/estimatedTime.summary: Saves the planned time for one person, task and day. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. A member may plan their own time only; planning for others needs an owner or admin role or the Everyone grant on the workload or project timesheet. The project must be one the caller can open, else 403. Reads `userId`, `taskId`, `projectId` (ids), `date` and `minutes` (a number from 0 to 1440) from the body, all required, plus `id` (the row id, to edit a row) and `timeZone`. Without `id` it creates the row or updates the one for that person, day and task. Answers with the saved row itself, not wrapped in `data`; bad input answers 400.

POST /api/v1/estimatedTime.summary: Runs a read query over planned time rows and returns the result. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `queryeta` (an aggregation pipeline) from the body. The query is limited to the rows and projects the caller may see, and a query that breaks that limit answers 400. Answers with the list of result rows itself, not wrapped in `data`.

POST /api/v1/estimatedTime/ai/:tid.summary: Asks the AI for an estimate of a task and saves it on the task. Needs a task the caller can open and the permission to change task estimated hours in its project, else 403. Reads `tid` (task id) from the path and `userId` and `userName` (strings) from the body. The task must have a description. Answers with `data`: `totalEstimatedTime`, `minutes`, `optimistic`, `likely`, `pessimistic`, `confidence`, `work_items`, `reasoning` and `basedOnSamples`. Failures give `status` false and a `statusText`.

POST /api/v1/estimatedTime/ai/:tid/propo.summary: Asks the AI for an estimate of a task without saving it. Needs a task the caller can open and the permission to change task estimated hours in its project, else 403. Reads `tid` (task id) from the path. The task must have a description. Answers with `data`: `minutes`, `optimistic`, `likely`, `pessimistic`, `confidence`, `work_items`, `reasoning`, `basedOnSamples` and `previousMinutes`. Failures give `status` false and a `statusText`.

GET /api/v1/timesheet/week.summary: Gives one person's week of logged time, grouped by task, with capacity and approval state. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Only an owner or admin may name another person with `userId`; for anyone else it is ignored. Reads `start` and `end` (dates, required, else 400), `userId`, `projectId`, `hoursPerDay` (a number, default 8) and `timeZone` from the query. Answers with `data`: `userId`, `zone`, `hoursPerDay`, `workingDays`, `days`, `rows`, `totals`, `underCapacity`, `approval` and `running`.

GET /api/v1/timesheet/task/:taskId.summary: Gives the time entries logged on one task. Needs a task the caller can open. Reads `taskId` from the path. The caller sees only their own entries, unless they hold the Everyone grant on the user timesheet for that project, then all. Answers with `data`: `taskId`, `estimateMinutes`, `totalMinutes`, `mineMinutes`, `seesEveryone` and `entries` (each with `userId`, `startedAt`, `endedAt`, `minutes`, `note`, `billable`, `source`, `running`, `locked` and `canEdit`). A bad id answers 400 and a missing task 404.

GET /api/v1/timesheet/hours-by-source.summary: Adds up the hours people logged, leaving out AI agent time. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Owners and admins get the whole company, others only their own hours. Reads `start` and `end` (Unix times in seconds) from the query, both optional. Answers with `data`: `peopleHours`, `entryCount`, `start`, `end` and `scope` (`company` or `self`).

PUT /api/v1/timesheet/entries/billable.summary: Marks time entries billable or not. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Owners and admins may change any entry; others only their own, and other entries are left alone. Reads `entryIds` (a list of ids, required, else 400) and `billable` (a boolean, anything but false counts as true) from the body. Answers with `statusText` `Billable updated.` and `data`: `updated` and `billable`.

POST /api/v1/timesheet/billable-summary.summary: Adds up billable and non-billable time over a period. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Owners and admins read the whole company and may filter by user; others read only their own time. Projects hidden from the caller are left out. Reads `userArray` (ids), `projectArray` (ids), `start` and `end` (Unix times in seconds, both needed to filter by date) from the body. Answers with `data`: the billable split plus `scope` (`company` or `self`).

POST /api/v1/timesheet/export-csv.summary: Exports time entries as a CSV file. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `userArray` (ids), `projectArray` (ids), `start` and `end` (Unix times in seconds, both needed to filter by date) from the body. Answers with a downloadable CSV file `timesheet-export.csv` with user, project, date, description, billable and hours. A failure answers 500 with the text `Export failed`.

POST /api/v1/timesheet/send-reminders.summary: Sends the log your time reminder emails now. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads nothing. It emails the chosen members who have not logged time today, only when reminders are switched on, there are chosen members and today is a working day. Answers with `statusText` `Reminders processed.` and `data`: `reminded`, `total`, `users` and, when nothing was sent, `skipped` with the reason.

GET /api/v1/timesheet/reminder-settings.summary: Reads the company's time reminder settings. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads the company header only. Answers with `data`: `settings`. Without the company header it answers 400.

PUT /api/v1/timesheet/reminder-settings.summary: Changes the company's time reminder settings. Only an owner or admin may call it, else 403. Reads `enabled` (a boolean) and `userIds` (a list) from the body; at least one is needed, else 400. Answers with `statusText` `Reminder settings updated.` and `data`: `settings`.

POST /api/v1/timesheet/rates.summary: Saves a billing rate. Only an owner or admin may call it, else 403. Reads `scope` and `rate` (required), `refId` (needed for scopes other than `default`) and `currency` (default `USD`) from the body. It updates the rate for that scope and `refId` or adds it. Answers with `statusText` `Rate saved.` and `data`: the saved rate; bad input gives `status` false.

POST /api/v1/updateunreadcommentscount.summary: Changes the signed-in user's unread count for a project, task, chat message, mention or notification. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, but only for their own counts: if `userIds` (array of ids) names anyone else it answers 403 with `statusText`. Reads `key` (number, required: 1 project, 2 task, 3 chat message, 4 mention, 5 notification), `read`, `set` and `readAll` (booleans), `messageCount` and `prevCount` (numbers), `projectId`, `sprintId`, `taskId`, `messageId` and `parentTaskId` (ids) from the body. Keys 1 and 2 need `projectId` and `userIds`, key 2 also needs `sprintId` and `taskId`, key 3 needs `messageId`, key 4 needs `readAll`. With `read`, `set` or `readAll` it changes only the caller's count; without them only keys 1, 2 and 4 are accepted, else 403. A `companyId` in the body that differs from the company header is refused. Answers with `status` and `data`: a message that the count was updated. A rejected request answers 400 with `statusText`.

POST /api/v1/pushupdateunreadcommentscou.summary: Changes the signed-in user's unread count for a project, task, chat message, mention or notification. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, but only for their own counts: if `userIds` (array of ids) names anyone else it answers 403 with `statusText`. Reads `key` (number, required: 1 project, 2 task, 3 chat message, 4 mention, 5 notification), `read`, `set` and `readAll` (booleans), `messageCount` and `prevCount` (numbers), `projectId`, `sprintId`, `taskId`, `messageId` and `parentTaskId` (ids) from the body. Keys 1 and 2 need `projectId` and `userIds`, key 2 also needs `sprintId` and `taskId`, key 3 needs `messageId`, key 4 needs `readAll`. With `read`, `set` or `readAll` it changes only the caller's count; without them only keys 1, 2 and 4 are accepted, else 403. A `companyId` in the body that differs from the company header is refused. Answers with `status` and `data`: a message that the count was updated. A rejected request answers 400 with `statusText`.

POST /api/v1/unsetCommentCounts.summary: Clears stored unread comment counts for a project or list. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and the code checks no project access or role. Reads `projectId` (id), `sprintId` (id), `searchKey` (string) and `companyId` (id) from the body. One of `projectId` or `searchKey` is required, else 400 with `statusText`. A `companyId` that differs from the company header answers 403. It removes the matching count fields for every user's count record in the company, not only the caller's. Answers with `status`, `statusText` (`success`) and `data`: the result of the bulk update. Failures answer 500 with `statusText`.

GET /api/v1/teams.summary: Lists the teams of the workspace. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads nothing from the request. Answers with the list of team records itself (no `data` wrapper), and sets a `FromCache` header when the list came from cache. Failures answer 500 with `message` and `error`.

POST /api/v1/teams/addTeam.summary: Creates a team. The caller needs the `settings.settings_create_team` permission, checked strictly, else 403 with `statusText`. Reads `name` (string, required), `value` (string, required), `teamColor` (object with `bgColor` and `color` strings, required) and `assigneeUsersArray` (list of user ids, each must be a member of the workspace) from the body. Any other field is refused. Answers with the saved team record itself. Bad input answers 400 with `statusText`, and other failures 500.

PUT /api/v1/teams/updateTeam.summary: Changes a team's name or colour, or adds or removes one member. The caller needs the `settings.settings_team_list` permission, checked strictly, else 403 with `statusText`. Reads `id` (team id, required), `key` (`$set`, `$addToSet` or `$pull`, required) and `updateObject` (object) from the body. With `$set`, `updateObject` may hold `name`, `value` (both strings) and `teamColor`. With `$addToSet` or `$pull`, it holds one `assigneeUsersArray` user id, and an added user must be a workspace member. Answers with the updated team record itself. Bad input answers 400 with `statusText`, and other failures 500.

GET /api/v1/members.summary: Lists the member rows of the workspace. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and the fields on each row depend on the caller: owners, admins and holders of `settings.settings_member_list` see seat details, others see a smaller set, and `userId` is hidden on rows that are not accepted yet. Reads nothing from the request. Answers with `data`: the member rows, and sets a `FromCache` header when cached. Failures answer 500.

GET /api/v1/members/:id.summary: Finds one member row by account id. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `id` (the member's user id) from the path. Managers of members can find any row of that account, everyone else only finds a live seat. Answers with the member row itself (no `data` wrapper), or an empty answer when none matches. Failures answer 500.

GET /api/v1/members/:key/:value.summary: Checks whether any member holds a given role or designation. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `key` (`roleType` or `designation`) and `value` (a whole number) from the path. Anything else answers 400 with `message`. Answers with `isUsed`: true when a member has it. Failures answer 500.

POST /api/v1/members/private-view.summary: Adds, changes or removes a private view saved on the caller's own member row. Any signed-in member may call it, but only on their own row, else 403 with `statusText`. Reads `id` (member row id, required), `data` (object, required), `operation` (`push`, `update`, `settings` or `delete`, required) and `key` (`name`, `title` or `isPin`, used with `update`) from the body. `update` and `settings` also need `data.id` (the view id) and the view must exist, else 404. Answers with `status` and `statusText` (`Private view saved.`). Bad input answers 400, an unknown row 404, and other failures 500. It also records a note in the project history when the view names a project the caller can read.

PUT /api/v1/members.summary: Changes fields on a member row, such as role, seat status, removal, manager or designation. Needs the `settings.settings_member_list` permission, except that any member may change their own `dashboardLocked` setting. Reads `id` (member row id, required) and `data` (object, required) from the body. Only an owner or admin can change another member or `managerId`. Only an owner can grant the owner or admin role or change an owner. Nobody can change their own role, and the last owner cannot be demoted or removed. Fields such as `userId`, `companyId` and `userEmail` cannot be changed, and `$` operators are refused. A manager must pass the reporting line check. Removing a member releases their seat and revokes their API tokens. Answers with `status`, `statusText` (`Member updated.`) and `data`: the updated row. Refusals answer 400, 403 or 404 with `statusText`, and other failures 500.

PUT /api/v1/root-members.summary: Lets an invited person accept their invitation to a company. The caller must be signed in, and either holds `settings.settings_member_list` or sends a body that only links their own account to the invitation. Reads `id` (invitation row id, required), `companyId` (id, required), `data` (object with `userId` and `status`, required) and `linkId` (string, the invitation link token) from the body. The `data.userId` must be the caller, `data.status` must be 2, and the invitation must still be pending, carry the right link and be sent to the caller's account or email. Answers with `status`, `statusText` (`Invitation accepted.`) and `data`: the seat row. Refusals answer 400, 401, 403 or 404 with `statusText`, and other failures 500.

POST /api/v1/members/count.summary: Counts member rows that match a simple filter. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `query` (object) from the body, which may use only `roleType`, `designation`, `status` and `isDelete`, each a string, number or boolean. Anything else answers 400 with `statusText`. Answers with a list holding `totalCount` (or an empty list when nothing matches), with no `data` wrapper. Failures answer 500.

POST /api/v1/comments.summary: Saves a new comment or reply on a project, list or task. The caller must be able to open that project, list and task, else 404 with `statusText`. Reads `data` (object, required) from the body, with `projectId`, `sprintId`, `taskId`, `message`, `mediaURL` and `parentId` (ids and text). The author is always the caller, whatever `userId` is sent. Mentions in `message` are found and notified, unread counts are raised and agents or AI may start when named. Answers with `status` and `data`: the saved comment, plus `ai` or `agents` when those started. Bad thread ids answer 400, and failures 500.

PUT /api/v1/comments.summary: Edits or soft-deletes a comment. The caller must be able to open its thread, else 404. Only the author or an owner or admin may change it, but any member may change only `pinnedMessage`, else 403 with `message`. Reads `id` (comment id, required), `data` (object of fields to set), `isProjectComment` (boolean) and `options` (only `timestamps`, a boolean) from the body. A comment cannot move to another thread or author, answering 400. Answers with `status` and `data`: the updated comment. Failures answer 500.

GET /api/v1/comments/get-paginated-messa.summary: Lists the top level comments of a project, list or task chat, newest first. The caller must be able to open the project, list and task, else 404 with `statusText`. Reads `projectId` (id, required), `taskId` (id), `sprintId` (id), `isDefault`, `mainChat` (booleans), `skipValue` and `batchLimit` (numbers, default 0 and 25) and `tabLeaveTime` (a timestamp in milliseconds) from the query. Answers with `data`: the comments, with a reply summary where threads apply. Failures answer 500.

GET /api/v1/comments/get-searched-messag.summary: Searches the messages of a project, list or task chat. The caller must be able to open the project, list and task, else 404 with `statusText`. Reads `projectId` (id, required), `sprintId` and `taskId` (ids), `searchText` (string, matched against message and file names), `isPinnedMessage` (`true` for pinned only), `skip` and `limit` (numbers, default 0 and 25) and `sort` (`asc` or `desc`) from the query. Answers with `data`: the matching comments. Failures answer 500.

GET /api/v1/comments/replies.summary: Lists the replies in one comment thread, oldest first. The caller must be able to open the thread's project, list and task, else 404 with `statusText`. Reads `parentId` (comment id, required, else 400) from the query. Answers with `data`: the replies, and `root`: the parent comment. Failures answer 500.

GET /api/v1/comments/action-items.summary: Lists the open assigned comments on one task, oldest first, up to 100. The caller must be able to open the task, else 404. Reads `taskId` (id, required, else 400), `projectId` (id) and `sprintId` (id) from the query. Answers with `data`: the comments. Failures answer 500.

GET /api/v1/comments/assigned-to-me.summary: Lists the open comments assigned to the caller, newest assignment first, up to 50. Only those on tasks and docs the caller can still open are returned. Reads nothing from the request. Answers with `data`: the comments, each with `taskName` and `taskKey` for task comments. Failures answer 500.

POST /api/v1/comments/assign.summary: Assigns a task comment to a member, or clears its assignee. The caller must be able to post to the task, else 404. Changing an existing assignment is allowed only to the comment's author, the one who assigned it, the current assignee or an owner or admin, else 403 with `statusText`. Reads `id` (comment id, required, else 400) and `assigneeId` (user id, empty to clear) from the body. The assignee must be an active person who can see the task, else 400. Answers with `status` and `data`: the updated comment. The new assignee is notified. Failures answer 500.

POST /api/v1/comments/resolve.summary: Marks an assigned task comment as resolved or open again. The caller must be able to open the task, else 404. Only the assignee, the person who assigned it or an owner or admin may do it, else 403 with `statusText`. Reads `id` (comment id, required, else 400) and `resolved` (boolean, true unless `false`) from the body. The comment must be assigned, else 400. Answers with `status` and `data`: the updated comment. Failures answer 500.
